items.title: Ambassador Smith urges investors to create well-paying jobs to curb brain drain
items.description: The Embassy of Ghana in the United States, in collaboration with Region 17, has held a special business roundtable in Chicago, Illinois, bringing together investors, business leaders and other stakeholders to explore investment opportunities and strengthen economic ties between Ghana and the United States. Ghana’s Ambassador to the United States, Victor Emmanuel Smith, underscored the importance of productive investment that creates sustainable, well-paying jobs for young people. He called for a shift from investments focused primarily on resource extraction to partnerships that promote local manufacturing, skills development, technology transfer, and the growth of Ghanaian enterprises. “I am not interested merely in investment that extracts resources and leaves little lasting value behind. I want investment that builds factories, investment that develops skills, investment that creates supply chains,” he stated. As a practical outcome of the engagement, the Ambassador proposed the establishment of a Ghana–Chicago Strategic Business Investment Partnership to connect interested companies, investors, diaspora professionals and relevant institutions. He identified agribusiness, advanced manufacturing, financial services, digital technology and aviation as five priority areas, proposing that within 90 days, stakeholders work towards identifying interested companies, developing an initial pipeline of investment opportunities and arranging follow-up engagements, including a possible business delegation to Ghana. The Ambassador also encouraged investors to consider Ghana as a gateway to the wider African market of approximately 1.4 billion people, highlighting opportunities in agricultural processing, cocoa value addition, food production, manufacturing and logistics. He particularly called for partnerships that would strengthen local supply chains and create opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises. Speaking at the event, Illinois State Senator for the 16th District, William Preston, highlighted the strong historical and cultural connections between Chicago and Ghana, stressing the need to translate these ties into meaningful economic partnerships. He identified opportunities in agriculture, manufacturing, technology, workforce development and education, and announced progress towards recruiting teachers from Ghana to help address teacher shortages in Illinois. He also pointed to the potential for local businesses, including Chicago-based Brown Sugar Bakery, to establish stronger commercial links with Ghana. Other participants shared experiences of successful diaspora-led investment initiatives, including a Chicago-based real estate entrepreneur who recounted bringing a delegation of 50 investors to Ghana for the organisation’s eighth annual conference, alongside local business owners and exhibitors. The experience, she noted, demonstrated the importance of connecting diaspora investors with businesses and entrepreneurs on the ground in Ghana. The roundtable reaffirmed the shared interest of Ghana and Illinois in building practical, mutually beneficial commercial relationships, with a focus on turning historical connections and investment discussions into lasting partnerships, business opportunities and jobs.

items.title: Hungarian authorities uncover $20m during probe of Orbán-era minister
items.description: Nearly $20m (£14.8m) in cash has been found hidden in farm buildings and buried in forests as part of an investigation into a former minister of Viktor Orbán, authorities have said. Miklós Seszták, who served as minister of national development for four of the ex-prime minister’s 16-year rule, is accused of accepting bribes as part of a scheme involving the state transport company. He has denied any wrongdoing. Hungary’s new Prime Minister Péter Magyar unseated Orbán in a landslide election in April on the promise of launching a sweeping anti-corruption drive. On Friday, following the two-day search for the cash – found in secluded locations across the country – Magyar described it as the end of the “mafia”. Investigators found wads of banknotes in safes, buried in woodlands and hidden in agricultural and residential buildings and warehouses, as part of the probe into Seszták, the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH) said in a statement. The cash amounted to “5,071,632,000 forints, €2,658,350 and $1,257,100”, it added, bringing the combined value to $19.5m. It has been deposited into the Hungarian State Treasury, the body said. The NVVH was established to investigate allegations of corruption during the Orbán rule, which Magyar has dubbed “Operation Purgatory”. Magyar promised Hungarians “regime change” during the election earlier this year and has set about undoing many Orbán-era policies since entering office. Allegations of corruption and cronyism have long dogged Orbán, who during the course of his tenure turned Hungary into what the EU characterised as an “electoral autocracy”. His government faced accusations of offering lucrative government projects to allies. Orbán has strongly denied the claims. Two of his former ministers, including Seszták, and the former central bank chief Gyorgy Matolcsyhave been under arrest since September over accusations of graft in separate investigations. They all deny wrongdoing. On Monday, Hungarian authorities also detained Orbán’s brother and three others as part of a people-smuggling case. The former prime minister ​dismissed it as political revenge, saying: “In this dirty game, ​the aim is the elimination of the political opponent and the establishment of a one-party system. “I am the target, my younger brother is just a tool.”

items.title: Marchés carbone: l’Alliance ouest-africaine veut positionner la sous-région au cœur de ce mécanisme
items.description: Seize États membres de l’Alliance ouest-africaine sur les marchés carbone et la finance climat ont célébré dix années de coopération et défini leurs nouvelles ambitions. Face à l’insuffisance des financements climatiques, la sous-région ambitionne de faire des marchés carbone un levier stratégique pour mobiliser des ressources, accélérer la transition écologique et financer ses engagements climatiques. TÜRKIYE – En marge de la Cop31, qui se tient à Antalya, en Türkiye, du 9 au 20 novembre, les 16 États membres de l’Alliance ouest-africaine sur les marchés carbone et la finance climat se sont réunis hier pour dresser le bilan de dix années d’existence de cette structure régionale et réfléchir à ses perspectives. Créée en 2016, l’Alliance est née d’un constat : une grande partie des engagements pris par les pays ouest-africains dans le cadre de leurs Contributions déterminées au niveau national (Cdn) reste tributaire de financements extérieurs. « À titre d’exemple, la Communauté économique des États de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (Cedeao) estime à environ 294 milliards de dollars les besoins de financement nécessaires à la mise en œuvre des Cdn de la sous-région d’ici à 2030. Or, entre 2019 et 2022, nos États n’ont mobilisé qu’environ 3,3 milliards de dollars sur les 82,7 milliards FCfa requis pour financer la composante conditionnelle de leurs Cdn, soit moins de 5 % », a déploré Ousmane Fall Sarr, coordonnateur de l’Alliance. Cette situation est d’autant plus préoccupante que l’aide publique au développement connaît un recul. Elle a ainsi diminué de 23 % en 2025, selon les données évoquées par le coordonnateur. « Les dons et les prêts concessionnels ne suffiront donc pas à combler le déficit de financement. C’est là que les marchés carbone prennent tout leur sens. Ils constituent aujourd’hui l’un des rares mécanismes capables d’attirer, à grande échelle, des capitaux privés vers l’action climatique en Afrique. Les opportunités sont réelles », a-t-il estimé. L’Afrique de l’Ouest dispose déjà d’acquis dans ce domaine. « Au total, 64,7 millions de tonnes de crédits carbone ont été émises dans nos pays et 343 projets ont été enregistrés sur le marché de l’union, dont 42 millions de tonnes issus de projets qui lui sont propres », a indiqué Ousmane Fall Sarr. Derrière ces chiffres, a-t-il souligné, se trouvent des communautés, notamment des femmes et des familles, dont les conditions de vie et la santé bénéficient des retombées de ces projets. Toutefois, l’accès aux marchés carbone n’est pas automatique. Il suppose la mise en place de cadres réglementaires solides, de systèmes crédibles et de crédits répondant à des exigences élevées d’intégrité. « Seuls les pays dotés de ces dispositifs pourront véritablement tirer profit de ces marchés. Aucun de nos États ne peut relever seul ce défi. Mais ensemble, nous pensons y arriver », a soutenu le coordonnateur. Dix ans de construction et de coopération régionale L’idée de mettre en place une telle structure a émergé en 2016. Dix ans plus tard, l’Alliance s’est progressivement imposée comme une institution régionale reconnue. Son évolution s’est articulée autour de trois grandes étapes, selon Ousmane Fall Sarr. De 2017 à 2019, les efforts ont porté sur la structuration, la mise en place de sa gouvernance, la constitution de son réseau de points focaux et l’établissement de mécanismes de coopération. Entre 2020 et 2024, l’accent a été mis sur la préparation des pays membres à la mise en œuvre de l’article 6 de l’Accord de Paris, à travers le renforcement des capacités, les échanges d’expériences entre pairs et l’assistance technique aux États. Depuis 2024, l’Alliance est entrée dans une nouvelle phase, consacrée à la mise en œuvre concrète des activités, avec un accompagnement renforcé au niveau de chaque pays membre. Prenant la parole au nom du ministre sénégalais de l’Environnement et de la Transition écologique, Cheikh Ndiaye Sylla a salué les dix années d’engagement de l’alliance. « C’était un pari difficile. Mais depuis sa création, elle a contribué à renforcer les capacités de nos États, à faciliter le partage d’expériences et à promouvoir une approche régionale des enjeux liés aux marchés carbone. Des projets ont émergé et des financements ont été mobilisés », a-t-il souligné. Pour lui, l’adoption de la Déclaration de Pointe-Sarène, en mai 2025, au Sénégal, illustre la volonté collective des États ouest-africains de franchir une nouvelle étape dans leur coopération. Cette déclaration repose sur dix engagements, portant notamment sur le renforcement des capacités nationales, l’harmonisation des cadres régionaux et le développement d’une plateforme commune de coopération sur les marchés carbone. Pour Cheikh Ndiaye Sylla, ces mécanismes représentent également une opportunité pour le Sénégal de diversifier ses sources de financement et de mobiliser des ressources supplémentaires en faveur de l’action climatique. De notre envoyé spécial à Antalya (Turquie), Ndiol Maka SECK

items.title: Kwankwaso’s daughter seeks divorce from Kano gov, offers to refund dowry
items.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The second wife of Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, Zainab Musa Kwankwaso, has filed for divorce at an Upper Area Court in Gudu, Abuja, offering to refund the dowry paid by the governor. Zainab, a daughter of former Kano State Governor Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, is seeking to dissolve the marriage through Khul’i, an Islamic procedure that allows a woman to seek divorce by returning her dowry or offering compensation. According to court documents, the court has summoned Governor Yusuf to appear on November 17, 2026, to respond to the suit. In her claim, Zainab cited a breakdown of the marriage, alleging a persistent lack of love, care, affection and emotional connection. She also told the court that efforts to reconcile them had failed and expressed willingness to refund the dowry paid on their wedding day. Zainab married Yusuf on July 29, 2006, and their marriage produced six children. Her divorce suit comes weeks after she reportedly left the Kano Government House for her father’s residence before travelling to Abuja. The post Kwankwaso’s daughter seeks divorce from Kano gov, offers to refund dowry appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: The Joy of True Mental Effort
items.description: This is an edition of The Wonder Reader, a newsletter in which our editors recommend a set of stories to spark your curiosity and fill you with delight. Sign up here to get it every Saturday morning. This past week, my colleague Lila Shroff recounted her experience at a “drunk deriving” party in San Francisco. The event is exactly what it sounds like: libations and collaborative attempts to solve math and logic problems. “The winning team will be the one with the highest combined blood-alcohol levels and exam score,” Lila writes. In Lila’s delightful story, she spends time with the people who remain devoted to the joy of doing math, even as AI transforms the field. Working with numbers means something different to each mathematician she speaks with—some delight in the purity of knowing there’s one right answer; for others, it’s the adrenaline rush of solving a problem. But one idea she returns to throughout the story is the togetherness of something like the drunk-deriving party. That kind of collaboration will become even more important as math evolves and becomes more accessible to the public, Lila writes. “Maybe the future is to be found in the drunk part of the drunk-math party—not in the encouragement of drunkenness itself, but in the partnership that I encounter when I ask my teammates for help.” Today’s newsletter explores how to fully engage the brain, and the value of doing that alongside other people. The Work of the Brain What I Learned at a Drunk-Math Party By Lila Shroff AI might be taking over mathematics research, but there is reason for hope when it comes to the uniquely human love of numbers. Read the article. The Puzzle That Will Outlast the World By A. J. Jacobs One move down, 1,298,074,214,633,706,907,132,624,082,305,022 to go. ( From 2022 ) Read the article. The People Who Will Thrive in the AI Age By David Brooks What will differentiate people is not how smart they are but their relationship to mental effort. Read the article. Still Curious? “My descent into mah-jongg” : The game seems to be everywhere, all at once, Ashley Parker writes. “What do crossword puzzles really test?” : In 2024, Sophia Stewart explored the case for puzzles that reflect a broader sense of common knowledge. Other Diversions Zelda ’s midlife crisis The writer who made food fun An offbeat director worth your time PS Courtesy of Andrea W. I recently asked readers to share a photo of something that sparks their sense of awe in the world. Andrea W. shared this photo of a butterfly “flitting from flower to flower. It was missing a huge chunk of one wing but was still going and was lovely as ever.” I’ll continue to feature your responses in the coming weeks. — Isabel

items.title: COP 31 : la région de Nouakchott expose son expérience en matière de lutte contre le changement climatique
items.description: La région de Nouakchott a présenté son expérience en matière de lutte contre le changement climatique, lors d’un événement qu’elle a organisé en marge de la 31e Conférence des Parties (COP31) à Antalya, en Turquie, sous le titre « La région de Nouakchott face au changement climatique : de la stratégie climatique à l’action de terrain au niveau territorial ». Dans un communiqué publié ce samedi, la région a indiqué que la rencontre avait abordé les principaux défis climatiques auxquels est confrontée la capitale, notamment les inondations, l’érosion côtière, la hausse des températures et la pression croissante sur les ressources en eau, ainsi que l’expansion urbaine galopante. Elle a ajouté que cet événement avait pour objectif de présenter les mesures qu’elle a prises pour renforcer la résilience et la capacité d’adaptation du territoire face à ces défis. Au cours de la réunion, la présidente de la région, Fatima mint Abdelmalek, a présenté la vision politique de la région, soulignant le rôle central joué par les autorités locales dans la mise en œuvre concrète des actions en faveur du climat, en complémentarité avec les politiques nationales et les engagements internationaux. Les interventions techniques ont également porté sur les synergies entre le plan régional de développement et le plan climatique de la région, ainsi que sur les moyens de traduire leurs orientations en actions concrètes dans les domaines prioritaires. La région de Nouakchott a réaffirmé son engagement à œuvrer pour la construction d’un territoire plus résilient et plus durable, soulignant l’importance des partenariats et de la coopération pour accélérer le rythme de l’action climatique au niveau local.

items.title: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says
items.description: US negotiators have touted the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership, Volodymyr Zelensky has said. The Ukrainian president’s comments come after President Donald Trump’s envoys met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Zelensky as part of US efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine. Kyiv has long sought membership of the military alliance, but this has previously been opposed by the US and others while Russia has said another Nato member on its border is unacceptable. Russia controls most of the industrial region of Donbas and Zelensky has consistently said Ukraine is unwilling to give up sovereign territory. Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. “The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’ This was the first time this had been raised,” Zelensky said in remarks released by his office on Saturday. He went on to say that if he received a proposal that contained security guarantees, no constraints on Ukraine’s military and funds to rebuild the country, he would put it to a referendum. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to the Irish capital, Dublin, on Thursday to meet Zelensky, after a round of talks with Putin in Moscow. Comments by both Putin and Kremlin officials suggest that Russia’s position on the war has not shifted, and that Moscow’s demands for territory and neutrality continue to far exceed what Ukraine is prepared to consider. Moscow has previously proposed limits on the size of Ukraine’s military, territorial concessions and Kyiv’s guaranteed neutrality as conditions of a peace deal. Ukraine has rejected these, arguing that such constraints would hamper its ability to stave off any future invasion. Russia has now raised the stakes further. It has revived 2021 demands for Nato to halt any expansion in Russia’s vicinity and to roll back military infrastructure from countries of central and eastern Europe which became Nato members following the dissolution of the Soviet Union. The US and other Western nations dismissed these demands then – and Moscow invaded Ukraine a few months later. However, questions of European security were on the agenda of the latest round of talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi this week. Russia has insisted it will not agree to cease fighting until a final peace deal is in place that would include territorial settlements as well as security arrangements. In the comments, made on Friday but only released on Saturday, Zelensky said that the US proposal made him believe that “Nato is back on the agenda”. But he cautioned: “You have also heard Putin’s signals, and this is an extremely difficult conversation.” Russia currently occupies roughly a fifth of Ukrainian territory, including most of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions that compose the Donbas. Ceding the small portions of land Ukraine still controls there would be symbolically significant for Kyiv. Zelensky has previously spoken of retaking Russian-controlled territory in four of Ukraine’s regions, as well as the Crimean peninsula, which Moscow annexed in 2014. The latest round of talks come after a period of fraught relations between Kyiv and Washington over Ukrainian strikes on oil facilities deep inside Russia, which Trump had asked Ukraine to pause to facilitate the supply of Russian diesel to ease global fuel prices. Zelensky then accused US officials of limiting Ukraine’s Starlink internet service, which it uses to co-ordinate defensive operations, while Trump said it was “time for Ukraine to get a new president” and called for fresh elections. Elections are suspended while Ukraine remains under martial law, but Zelensky has previously said he was willing to hold them within months of a peace deal being reached and would give up the presidency in exchange for Nato membership.

items.title: Here’s the latest.
Déjà sorcier à… 23 ans (Le billet de Omar DIOUF)
items.description: Sacrés Navétanes. On voit du tout dans ces championnats de football amateurs joués dans nos villes et villages durant les vacances scolaires, souvent de juillet à octobre ou novembre. Leur charme, comme à la lutte traditionnelle, le côté mystique et folklorique. Toute une armada de charlatans y est souvent déployée pour terrasser l’équipe adverse. C’est dans cette aventure mystique qu’un soi-disant « marabout », âgé juste de 23 ans, s’est embarqué avec l’équipe Asc Avenir pour vaincre leurs adversaires de l’Asc Relais, lors d’une finale zonale. Payé 100.000 FCfa pour sa prestidigitation, le jeune sorcier aurait débarqué au stade Caroline Faye de Mbour avec un linceul, en réalité un mannequin féminin en silicone enroulé dans du tissu, porté par trois quidams tous vêtus de rouge. Au finish, leur équipe a été bien corrigée par l’adversaire sur le score sans appel de 2 buts à 0. Et un malheur ne venant jamais seul, le magicien et ses trois acolytes ont été embarqués par la police et présentés à un juge. Curieux de savoir si le jeune parviendra à « envoûter » tout ce monde et sauver sa réputation. Une affaire à suivre… omar.diouf@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Le sport et la santé, ces nouveaux outils du soft power chinois (Par Oumar NDIAYE)
items.description: Même si elle est en avance par rapport aux autres concurrents sur la course à la coopération avec l’Afrique, la Chine n’entend pas laisser aussi le terrain de soft power. Premier partenaire économique de l’Afrique, les échanges commerciaux entre la Chine et le continent africain ont atteints, en 2025, plus de 300 milliards de dollars. Sur le plan politique, les connexions institutionnelles sont de haut niveau de la par le Forum de coopération sino-africaine (Focac) qui est la rencontre de ce genre à enregistrer la plus grande présence de chefs d’État et de gouvernement. En parallèle, la Chine est en train de développer un soft power, une politique d’influence douce pour asseoir son influence. Popularisé le politologue américain Joseph Nye, le concept de soft power est définit comme l’habileté d’obtenir ce que l’on désire par l’attraction et la séduction plutôt que par la coercition ou les paiements. Dans son ouvrage « Soft Power : The means to success in word politics » (Soft Power : les moyens deréussir en politique étrangère, PublicAffairs Edition), publié en 2004, Joseph Nye détaillait ainsi les éléments qui fondent la politique de persuasion des États-Unis, qui n’ont rien à voir avec la puissance militaire ou économique. La Chine, avec sa puissance économique et même militaire, utilise ainsi ces outils de persuasion pour davantage se rapprocher des populations des zones avec qui elle développe une coopération historique et dynamique. Parmi ces outils, le sport est l’un des meneurs de jeu. La dernière polémique de Kylian Mbappé avec ce que les Chinois considèrent comme un dérapage a révélé plusieurs choses à la fois. D'abord, la diplomatie du loup guerrier (wolf warrior) est toujours active en Chine avec un esprit conquérant et surtout décomplexé. Ensuite, depuis quelques années, les entreprises chinoises sont de plus en plus présentes dans le sponsoring des compétitions sportives continentales et internationales, et aussi dans plusieurs grands championnats dont la « Liga » espagnole et la « Premier League » anglaise. Il y a aussi l'énorme marché chinois, véritable niche pour les diffusions des compétitions sportives. Sans être une puissance sportive de grande envergure, malgré que sa capitale Beijing ait une particularité rare dans le monde du sport et de l’olympisme en organisant les Jeux Olympiques d’été en 2008 et d’hiver en 2022, la Chine a déployé ses ailes dans le sponsoring des grands événements sportifs. À la dernière Coupe d’Europe des nations 2024, sur les 13 sponsors mondiaux, 5 sont des compagnies chinoises dont le géant de l’automobile électrique BYD ou le service de paiement AliPay. L’ampleur de « l’affaire Kylian Mbappé » et ses développements avec l’avalanche d’excuses présentées par l’international français, son club le Real de Madrid, et l’instance dirigeante du championnat espagnol, la « Liga », démontre ainsi la place et le poids occupés par le marché chinois sur le « merchandising » dans le domaine du sport, principalement le football. Sans compter que ce pays est devenu incontournable en devenant constructeur de stades dans beaucoup régions du monde, surtout en Afrique. Selon des estimations relayées par plusieurs médias chinois, les revenus publicitaires de Kylian Mbappé en Chine sont de 22 millions d’euros (plus de 14 milliards de Fcfa) par an, soit 38 % de ses revenus commerciaux mondiaux. Ce n’est pas seulement dans le sport que la Chine entend dérouler sa politique d’influence douce. Dans le domaine de la santé aussi, même si ces missions médicales ont lontemps sillonné l’Afrique des profondeurs, la Chine envoie aussi des navires-hopitaux faire des consultations dans beaucoup de pays africains. Le navire-hôpital « Arche du bonheur » a accosté en Mauritanie, au Sénégal, en Guinée, en Côte d’Ivoire, au Togo et au Ghana entre les mois d’octobre et novembre. Lors de son passage à Dakar, du 25 septembre au 1er octobre, ce bâtiment a effectué plus 6000 consultations et aussi 29 chirurgies. Ainsi avec ces outils que sont le sport et la santé, la Chine est en train d’étendre son influence en répondant aux besoins des populations locales, tout en gardant son avance sur la coopération dans plusieurs zones géographiques telles que l’Afrique… oumar.ndiaye@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Le parti Tewassoul appelle le gouvernement à corriger les déséquilibres des accords de pêche antérieurs avec l’UE
items.description: Le Parti du rassemblement national pour la réforme et le développement (Tewassoul) a estimé que la contribution financière offerte à la Mauritanie au titre de l'accord de pêche avec l'Union européenne est limitée et ne correspond ni à la valeur réelle de ses richesses marines, ni au volume des recettes tirées par les bénéficiaires de leur exploitation. Dans un communiqué publié ce samedi, le parti a déclaré que l’expiration du protocole d’application de l’accord constituait une occasion de réévaluer la politique d’exploitation des ressources halieutiques et de corriger les déséquilibres qui ont caractérisé les accords précédents. Il a appelé le gouvernement à aborder les négociations en cours de préparation dans un esprit de responsabilité nationale, à ne faire aucune concession portant atteinte aux droits souverains du pays, et à faire des garanties environnementales et des conditions d’exploitation durable des lignes rouges non négociables. Il a également demandé que les Mauritaniens puissent bénéficier davantage des richesses marines, en renforçant l’approvisionnement des marchés locaux en produits de la mer, en favorisant l’emploi national, en modernisant la flotte nationale et en développant les installations et les infrastructures liées au secteur de la pêche. Le parti a appelé les forces politiques, les organisations de la société civile, les experts et les chercheurs à se mobiliser autour de ce dossier, en exigeant que l’exploitation des richesses nationales fasse l’objet d’un débat national large et transparent, permettant à l’opinion publique de prendre connaissance de la réalité des accords, de leurs conditions, de leur efficacité et des retombées qu’ils génèrent pour le pays. C’est ce samedi soir que prend fin la validité du protocole d’application de l’accord de partenariat dans le domaine de la pêche entre la Mauritanie et l’Union européenne, qui remonte à 1987, alors que les deux parties ne sont pas parvenues à s’entendre sur un nouveau protocole, malgré plusieurs cycles de négociations menés ces derniers mois en vue de sa mise à jour.

items.title: Microsoft announces service ‘restored,’ global outage over
items.description: Tech giant Microsoft said Saturday it has “restored service” to customers, effectively drawing a close to a massive outage that caused chaos and disrupted public services and business around the world. “We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” the US-based company said in an X post. Microsoft had already reported a “broad recovery” for Outlook email and other services the day before, stating the major disruption was due to a technical issue and “not related to cyber or AI/agents.” The outage swept the globe on Thursday, taking the company’s products offline in at least 74 countries and territories across the Americas, Europe, Asia and Africa, according to the monitoring site Downdetector. Microsoft had attributed the disruption to “elevated load” on its infrastructure. It said the stoppage affected its Outlook email service, as well as Microsoft’s Teams communication platform and the company’s Copilot AI assistant. The post Microsoft announces service ‘restored,’ global outage over appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Et si on s’intéressait à la souffrance des hommes ? (Par Matel BOCOUM)
items.description: La communauté internationale s’apprête à célébrer, du 25 novembre au 10 décembre, les 16 jours d’activisme contre les Violences basées sur le genre (Vbg). Une nouvelle occasion de tirer la sonnette d’alarme face aux violences dont les femmes et les enfants sont généralement les principales victimes. Cette campagne invite à rendre visible ce qui demeure invisible. Pour autant, les projecteurs se braquent rarement sur ces hommes qui souffrent en silence, contraints à la résignation par le poids des étiquettes sociales et des exigences qui les poussent à tout endurer sans jamais se plaindre.Dire qu’ils sont de plus en plus nombreux à oser sortir de leur mutisme dans un cadre informel. Ils expriment les souffrances qu’ils disent vivre au sein de leur foyer, parfois du fait de leur épouse. Sur les réseaux sociaux, certaines publications révèlent ainsi une réalité souvent occultée. Derrière l’image de l’homme fort, protecteur et responsable de famille se cache parfois un être humain épuisé. Lui aussi a besoin d’écoute, de reconnaissance, de repos et de soutien au sein de son couple et de sa famille. Dans une publication sur Facebook, un auteur, sous le sceau de l’anonymat, attire l’attention sur le stress auquel est confrontée la gent masculine. Mais des hommes n’osent pas en parler, comme si la société les privait de ce droit. Leur quotidien est souvent marqué par des tensions conjugales, un manque de reconnaissance et une absence de soutien, autant de facteurs susceptibles d’accentuer leur mal-être. Dans ce sillage, l’expérience vécue en 2003 par la journaliste américaine Norah Vincent continue de susciter des réflexions. Elle avait fait une immersion dans le monde masculin sous l’identité fictive de « Ned ». Elle avait choisi de se faire passer pour un homme en modifiant son apparence physique. Alors qu’elle s’attendait à découvrir les privilèges masculins, la journaliste a été confrontée à une réalité qui l’a profondément bouleversée. Au terme de cette expérience de 18 mois, elle a traversé une grave dépression qui a nécessité une hospitalisation. Elle a ensuite relaté cette immersion dans un ouvrage intitulé Self-Made Man, publié en 2006. Il faut rappeler que cette journaliste, chroniqueuse reconnue notamment au Los Angeles Times et au Village Voice, avait l’habitude de bousculer les idées reçues. « Elle découvre une pression constante, invisible, que la société exerce sur les hommes. L’obligation d’être forts en permanence. L’interdiction tacite de montrer leur vulnérabilité. L’isolement émotionnel que beaucoup d’hommes vivent comme une fatalité. Ce que des chercheurs en psychologie documentent depuis des années sur la solitude masculine, Norah le vit dans sa chair », souligne un article en ligne attribué à TDN et daté du 15 avril 2026. Dans son livre Self-Made Man, publié en 2006, elle ne dresse pas un réquisitoire contre les hommes. Elle raconte avoir découvert que la vie masculine est bien plus dure qu’elle ne l’imaginait. Par ailleurs, si certains estiment que les difficultés rencontrées par les hommes dans leur vie quotidienne et conjugale pourraient expliquer leur espérance de vie plus faible que celle des femmes, les travaux scientifiques mettent en évidence plusieurs facteurs, notamment biologiques, génétiques, comportementaux et sociaux. Un article publié en mars 2020 sur le site Sciences et Avenir, suggère d’aborder la question de la différence d’espérance de vie entre les hommes et les femmes sous l’angle génétique. Il cite le bilan démographique de l’Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques (Insee) pour l’année 2019, les enfants nés cette année-là pouvaient espérer vivre en moyenne 85,6 ans pour les filles et 79,7 ans pour les garçons. L’article souligne que cet écart pourrait notamment s’expliquer par les comportements masculins : « les hommes prennent davantage de risques, exercent plus souvent certains métiers dangereux et adoptent parfois des habitudes de vie moins favorables à leur santé, ce qui peut augmenter leurs risques de développer des maladies cardiovasculaires ». Toutefois, ces écrits renseignent une souffrance masculine qui mérite, elle aussi, d’être entendue et prise en considération. matel.bocoum@lesoleil.sn

items.title: 2027: We won’t allow religion to divide us, Makinde declares
items.description: …seeks Muslim community’s support for Adekanmbi By Adeola Badru Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), ‘Seyi Makinde, has declared that his administration will not allow religious differences to divide the people of the state, insisting that they share a common ancestry and must remain united irrespective of their faith. Makinde, who made the declaration on Saturday, also appealed to Muslim leaders across the state to use their influence to promote unity, peace and political stability ahead of the 2027 general elections. The governor spoke at the opening of a three-day conference for Imams, Alfas/Ulama, political office holders and traditional rulers, tagged Rabitah 2026, organised by the League of Imams and Alfas in Yoruba Land (Rabitah tul Aimma wal Hulammai fii Biladi Yoruba) at the Jogor Event Centre, Ibadan. The conference, with the theme, “The Responsibilities of Politicians and Electorate During and After Electoral Process,“ brought together prominent Islamic clerics, scholars, traditional rulers and political stakeholders from across the South-West. Makinde noted that discussions surrounding the choice of the next governor of the state had intensified ahead of the elections, urging political and religious stakeholders not to allow such developments to create divisions along religious lines. “We won’t allow religion to divide us. Let us pray for our state and country because this is the period leading to the next election, when a new set of leaders will emerge.“ “There is a lot of discussion going on right now about the choice of who will become the next governor.“ “What matters most is that we must stay united. The progress of Oyo State is what is important to us, and I believe God will answer our prayers. For us in Oyo State, religion is not an issue.“ “We have all religions in our various families, and we have always coexisted peacefully,” he said. Makinde further illustrated the historical and familial connections between Muslims and Christians in Oyo State, disclosing that his own family background reflected the religious diversity he was advocating. He said: “I, standing before you, am Oluseyi Makinde. “Makinde was my grandfather on my father’s side. My father’s name is Olatunbosun, and my grandfather, Makinde, lived and died as a Muslim. Those who are familiar with Oyo know this history.“ “If I were to convene an extended family meeting this evening, about 65 per cent of those who would attend would be Muslims.“ “I want to appeal to us that we must not allow ourselves to be divided along religious lines because we share the same ancestry and the same blood flows through our veins.” The governor urged participants at the conference to use the gathering to pray for the continued peace and development of the state, stressing that religious differences should not undermine the bonds that unite the people. “Therefore, as this conference progresses, let us pray and work towards sustaining our unity. We must continue to recognise that we are one, irrespective of our religious differences,” he added. He also cautioned Muslim clerics against allowing individuals to exploit religious sentiments to create confusion and division during the forthcoming electoral process. Makinde urged them to deploy their influence towards promoting peaceful participation, tolerance and responsible political engagement, rather than allowing religious identity to become a tool for political manipulation. In support of the conference, the governor announced a donation of N50 million to the organisers, describing the gathering as an important platform for religious engagement and collective prayers for the state and the country. He also called on Muslim clerics and traditional religious leaders to play a constructive role in the 2027 electoral process, noting that they would have a significant opportunity to engage voters before they make their choices at the polls. According to him, political office-seekers and candidates would inevitably approach religious leaders and worship centres to solicit prayers and support as the elections draw closer. “As the Lord has designed the democratic process, the 2027 elections are approaching. Irrespective of what happens during the political process, you, as religious leaders, will have the final opportunity to interact with the electorate before they cast their votes.“ “Politicians and political candidates will visit your various mosques to seek prayers and support ahead of the elections.“ “I therefore urge you to use that opportunity to appeal to the people to support us and, more importantly, to pray for Nigeria,” Makinde said. Meanwhile, the League of Imams and Alfas in Yoruba Land declared that it will neither endorse nor declare support for any politician or political party ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Chairman of the League’s Board of Trustees, Sheikh Muhammad Habibullah Adam Abdullahi El-Ilory, said the organisation could not announce any preferred candidate or political platform ahead of the forthcoming elections. He stressed that Islamic clerics were not politicians and that their responsibility was not to campaign for political office-seekers or parties but to pray for the emergence of credible leaders. “We are religious leaders; we are not politicians, but we are the fathers of politicians. We will not declare support for any political party or politicians.“ “We, the League of Imams and Alfas in Yorubaland, cannot declare support or announce our support for any politician or political party. We can only pray to God for Him to give us credible leaders,” he said. The League’s President, Sheikh Jamiu Kewulere, also maintained that religious leaders should concentrate on their spiritual responsibilities rather than become involved in partisan political activities. According to him, Imams and Islamic clerics were expected to guide the people, promote moral values and preach Islam in accordance with its principles. “We are not politicians. An Imam is not supposed to be involved in politics. Our focus should be to guide people and preach the religion of Islam in line with Islamic principles,” he said. Similarly, the Grand Mufti of Yoruba Land, Sheikh AbdulRasaq AbdulAzeez Ishola, explained that the conference was convened to strengthen unity, understanding and cooperation among Muslims across Yorubaland before, during and after the 2027 general elections. He said the gathering was also designed to encourage religious leaders, political office holders and traditional institutions to appreciate their responsibilities in sustaining peace and democratic stability. The conference was attended by the APM governorship candidate in Oyo State, Abimbola Adekanmbi; his running mate, Mr Open Salawu; and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate, Alhaji Hazeem Gbolarumi. Also present were the League’s President, Sheikh Jamiu Kewulere; Chief Imam of Ibadanland, Sheikh Abdulganiy Abubakar; Alfa Agba of Ibadanland, Sheikh Abdulbari Adetunji; Grand Mufti of Yoruba Land, Sheikh AbdulRasaq AbdulAzeez Ishola; Secretary-General of the League, Sheikh Mustapha Oseni Adewale Hamzat; Chairman, Oyo State Pilgrim Welfare Board (Muslim Wing), Sheikh Hashim Atere; and Professor Kamil Olosho. Others included the Aare Musulumi of Yorubaland, Alhaji Daud Akinola; the Soun of Ogbomosoland, Oba Afolabi Olaoye; the Onigbeti of Igbeti, Oba Bashir Abioye; and the Iyalode Adini of Yorubaland, Alhaja Sedeekat Aderibigbe, alongside other prominent Islamic clerics, scholars and Muslim faithful from Oyo, Osun, Ogun, Ekiti, Lagos and Ondo states. The opening ceremony also featured lectures delivered by two university professors, Professor Amidu Sanni and Professor Adam Surajudeen, who addressed participants on issues relating to the responsibilities of political leaders and the electorate during and after elections. The conference is expected to provide a platform for discussions on the role of religious institutions, political office holders, traditional rulers and citizens in ensuring peaceful elections, responsible leadership and national development. items.title: Les « Jakaarka », pourvoyeurs d’emploi et de mort (Par Ibrahima Khaliloullah NDIAYE)
items.description: J’assistais, lundi dernier, à quelques encablures de mon bureau, à la mise sous terre d’un jeune homme, mécano de son état, dans le cimetière contigu au journal «Le Soleil» où reposent d’ailleurs de nombreux collègues et confrères. C’était après le crépuscule. Dans la pénombre, les lampes des téléphones portables furent allumées. Je pus apercevoir aisément les nombreuses silhouettes qui tinrent à accompagner le jeune homme à sa dernière demeure. Décédé la veille, le défunt, la quarantaine, était connu dans la zone où il habitait et faisait valoir son savoir-faire de mécano. Il a perdu la vie suite à un accident de moto dont la personne rescapée qui était avec lui, garde de sérieuses blessures.La moto ? Les « Jakarta » ? Une véritable hécatombe qui n’en finit pas. Pas un jour sans accident sur nos routes. Ces engins de la mort se faufilent, bifurquent, doublent sans prévenir. Sans aucun respect du Code de la route. La plupart de ceux qui les conduisent, des jeunes à la fleur de l’âge, ne connaissent d’ailleurs rien à la réglementation routière. Ils n’en ont cure. Ce qui les intéresse, c’est d’arriver à destination. Souvent, montrer leur aptitude à conduire par différentes girouettes ces motos qui ne cessent d’augmenter dans la circulation routière. C’est donc dans une totale irresponsabilité que voguent certains de ces jeunes, pris par l’allégresse de la vitesse et s’en donnant à cœur joie. L’évidence est qu’une éducation à la conduite s’impose à tous les usagers de la route, au-delà des « Jakartamen » aujourd’hui. Au moment où le job de conducteur de « Jakarta » est au hit-parade des pourvoyeurs d’emploi, l’État devrait organiser davantage le secteur. La première chose étant d’assurer la sécurité des usagers, des passagers et des piétons. Les tentatives d’immatriculation et de dotation de cartes grises, prolongées de paiement de taxes, n’ont pas trop arrangé les choses. Même le port de casque n’est pas systématique malgré de régulières opérations des forces de l’ordre affectées à la circulation sur cette défaillance particulière. Au Rwanda ou encore au Bénin, entre autres exemples en Afrique, le réflexe premier du transporteur est de donner le casque au transporté. Inutile de préciser que lui-même est le premier à en porter. Pour en revenir à l’accident évoqué ci-dessus, je me suis toujours étonné de la conduite irraisonnée des jeunes de Yarakh qui, au-delà de la maîtrise de la moto, versent, depuis des années, dans le spectacle au prix de leur vie. Sous les acclamations et ovations de leurs camarades. En attendant qu’un autre prenne le tour pour montrer ses talents de « cabreur » ou procède à un « laisser-deux » (les deux mains hors du guidon et ne tenant plus la moto). Les piétons font aussi les frais des conducteurs qui se prennent pour les « rois de la route ». Jusque sur les trottoirs ou les passages cloutés qu’ils sont supposés traverser en toute sécurité… Tel ce jeune homme victime d’un motocycliste pilotant une grosse cylindrée. La jeune fille que le chauffard transportait s’écria au moment du choc : « Oh, tu as tué le fils d’autrui ». Le conducteur n’eut rien d’autre à faire que de prendre la poudre d’escampette avant l’arrivée des passants qui se mirent à affluer. Le jeune blessé traîne encore les séquelles de l’accident et le plâtre enlevé de sa jambe ne signifie pas encore une guérison totale. Trois mois après l’accident, il marche encore difficilement et sa jambe droite tient grâce à un fer qui y est introduit. Le chauffard-fuyard, lui, vit certainement libre, mais avec un éternel remords en guise de tourment. À Thiès, c’est un enseignant, brillant prof de maths de son état, qui a été victime de la furie d’une moto alors qu’il était sur un trottoir. Les remords du motard et sa tentative de participer aux frais d’hospitalisation, refusée du reste, n’y changent rien. Malgré sa fracture de la hanche, notre prof n’a pas manqué de faire des remontrances à son « assassin de la mobilité » à qui il reprochait de priver ses potaches de leur enseignant, alors que certains d’entre eux sont en classe d’examen. Le mal est devenu tellement endémique que dans chaque grand hôpital, il existe une « salle Jakarta » où sont hospitalisées les nombreuses victimes d’accidents de deux-roues. Quant aux vieilles personnes, s’il y a un cauchemar qu’elle redoute quand elles sortent de leur maison, ce sont bien les « Jakarta », en raison de leur vitesse excessive et leur propension à les heurter n’importe où. Les motos se révèlent donc aujourd’hui un problème de santé et de sécurité publiques. Pas que. D’esthétique également. La ville de Saint-Louis, qui avait refusé les « Jakarta » jusqu’à récemment, a fini par accepter leur envahissement avec tout le lot de désordre qu’induisent ces engins de la mort. Et de pollution. Qu’elles puent les fumées de motos ! Parfois jusque dans nos maisons quand une en traverse à côté de nos fenêtres… À la décharge de ces jeunes, dont certains sont diplômés, les motos constituent aujourd’hui le secteur le plus grand pourvoyeur d’emplois pour eux. Cependant, ils restent, pour la plupart, piégés par la facilité du gain qu’elles offrent. L’émigration irrégulière par voie maritime se conjugue quelquefois avec la mort. Les motos, elles, donnent parfois la mort mais pas seulement à ceux qui choisissent de les conduire. Elles tuent et blessent aussi — et c’est là que le bât blesse — d’innocentes personnes qui n’ont eu que le tort de se retrouver sur leur chemin. L’équation qu’elles posent est très délicate. Comment concilier l’exigence de la débrouille urbaine pour ces innombrables jeunes qui en vivent et celle de sécurité pour les paisibles citoyens ? Une chose est sûre : il faudra bien attaquer, un jour, le mal par la racine. Et pourquoi ne pas commencer par tarir progressivement la source ? Faire en sorte que ces motos, pour l’essentiel de seconde main, entrent en bien moindres quantités sur le territoire national… ibrahimakhalil.ndiaye@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Pas de prime, pas de garantie : application de l'article 13 du Code CIMA Aux entreprises privées, aux entreprises et organismes publics, aux particuliers et à toute personne morale ou physique qui détient ou viendra à détenir un contrat d'assurance.
items.description: Sous l'égide de la Fédération des Sociétés d'Assurances de Droit National Africaines (FANAF), le 12e Forum des Marchés s'est tenu à Lomé les 2 et 3 novembre 2026. Il a réuni les dirigeants des sociétés d'assurance, les associations nationales, la Fédération Interafricaine des Assureurs Conseils (FIAC), les représentants des Directions Nationales des Assurances et le Secrétariat Général de la Conférence Interafricaine des Marchés d'Assurances (CIMA). Dans ses résolutions, le Forum a réaffirmé que la garantie d'un contrat d'assurance ne prend effet qu'après le paiement de la prime. Il a appelé l'ensemble des acteurs à une application stricte et simultanée de l'article 13 du Code CIMA dans tous les États membres de la CIMA. Le présent communiqué en précise les modalités pratiques pour les sociétés d'assurance, les intermédiaires d'assurance, les souscripteurs et les assurés. Le paiement préalable de la prime : une exigence légale au service des assurés L'article 13 du Code des assurances des États membres de la CIMA subordonne la prise d'effet du contrat au paiement de la prime. Il interdit aux sociétés d'assurance de souscrire ou de renouveler un contrat dont la prime n'est pas payée. La réglementation n'admet de délai de paiement que dans des cas limités et sous conditions, pour les risques de l'État et de ses démembrements et pour certains risques importants. À l'expiration de ces délais, le contrat non payé est résilié de plein droit. Cette règle protège les assurés. Les sinistres sont réglés avec les primes encaissées. Une prime non payée fait supporter le coût de la garantie par les assurés qui paient et réduit la trésorerie dont les sociétés d'assurance disposent pour faire face à leurs engagements envers les assurés et les victimes. Dispositions prises par les sociétés d'assurance en présence des régulateurs lors du Forum des Marchés Sous réserve des délais de paiement admis par la réglementation, les sociétés d'assurance membres de la FANAF et de l'APSAB appliquent les dispositions suivantes . aucun document d'assurance (police, avenant, attestation d'assurance automobile ou carte d'assurance maladie) n'est délivré avant le paiement intégral de la prime correspondante ; en assurance santé, aucune incorporation n'est intégrée dans la police et aucune carte d'assurance maladie n'est délivrée à l'assuré incorporé avant le paiement préalable de la prime d'incorporation la date d'effet de la garantie ne peut être antérieure à la date de paiement de la prime aucun contrat n'est renouvelé sans le paiement de la prime de la nouvelle période ; l'avis d'échéance est adressé à l'assuré au moins quarante-cinq (45) jours avant l'échéance ; en assurance santé et en assurance des risques divers, la souscription d'un contrat auprès d'une nouvelle société d'assurance est subordonnée à la présentation, au titre de la déclaration du risque, d'une attestation de non-redevance délivrée par la société d'assurance précédente. Celle-ci la délivre gratuitement dans un délai de cinq (5) jours ouvrés suivant la demande. L'attestation porte sur les seules primes échues et non payées un contrat dont la prime n'est pas payée à l'expiration du délai de paiement admis par la réglementation est résilié de plein droit ; un chèque ou un effet revenu impayé doit être régularisé dans les huit (8) jours ouvrés suivant la réception de la mise en demeure, faute de quoi le contrat est résilié de plein droit les primes sont payées, soit en espèces aux caisses de la société d'assurance, soit par chèque libellé à l'ordre de la société d'assurance, soit par virement, paiement électronique ou mobile money, directement sur les comptes de la société d'assurance les primes d'un montant inférieur ou égal à un (1) million de FCFA par police peuvent être encaissées en espèces par les intermédiaires, qui les reversent à la société d'assurance selon les procédures et délais fixés par celle-ci, dans un délai maximum de trente (30) jours suivant l'encaissement , Dispositions attendues des souscripteurs et des assurés Entreprises et organismes publics : payer la prime avant la prise d'effet du contrat. Les services et organismes relevant de la comptabilité publique paient la prime dans le délai maximal fixé par la Commission Régionale de Contrôle des Assurances (CRCA). À son expiration, le contrat non payé est résilié de plein droit. Les entreprises publiques qui ne relèvent pas de la comptabilité publique paient leur prime dans les mêmes conditions que les entreprises privées. Entreprises privées, particuliers et tout autre assuré : payer intégralement la prime avant la prise d'effet du contrat, selon l'un des modes de paiement indiqués ci-dessus, exiger une quittance ou un reçu officiel et conserver la preuve du paiement. Des dispositions d'application immédiate Ces dispositions s'appliquent dès à présent à tous les contrats souscrits ou renouvelés. Le principe n'est pas nouveau. Il découle de l'article 13 du Code CIMA, dans sa rédaction issue du règlement n o 0001/ClMA/PCMA/PCE/2011 du Conseil des Ministres de la CIMA du 11 avril 201 1. L'attestation de nonredevance en assurance santé et en assurance des risques divers en assure l'effectivité : elle empêche qu'une prime impayée auprès d'une société d'assurance soit suivie d'une nouvelle garantie auprès d'une autre. Un engagement partagé La FANAF et l'APSAB comptent sur l'engagement de chacun, clients, intermédiaires et sociétés d'assurance, pour la bonne application de ces dispositions. Pour toute question, chaque client peut s'adresser à sa société d'assurance, à son intermédiaire ou à l'APSAB. Fait à Dakar et à Ouagadougou, le 13 novembre 2026

items.title: ‘It’s unfortunate’ – Melaye reacts to Galadima’s claim on Justice Lifu’s illness
items.description: Dino Melaye has described as unfortunate elder statesman Buba Galadima’s comments linking him to discussions surrounding the health of Federal High Court judge, Justice Peter Lifu. Melaye said he never made any comment about Lifu’s health, noting “I was extremely shocked to hear that Alhaji Buba Galadima mentioned that I made comments on Justice Lifu’s health. “It is most unfortunate because I never made any comment on Justice Lifu’s health. “Old age must be catching up with Buba Galadima. Now I know you can’t cure old age, you can only manage it,” he wrote on his X (Twitter) page. Galadima had criticised members of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, over their reported reaction to Lifu’s health. In an interview on African Independent Television, AIT, on Wednesday, Galadima mentioned Melaye while referring to information that the ADC had obtained a certified true copy of the judgment delivered against the party. Galadima, a chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, said: “You know there was a judgment against ADC, isn’t it? Yes. And I’ve just heard you read something that Dino Melaye said. “They’ve got a true certified copy of the judgment, and I know some ADC people are jumping up and down that the judge (Peter Lifu) who gave a ruling against them has fallen ill and is supposed to be taken to hospital in Europe. “I just found out that maybe there aren’t intelligent people in the ADC. They didn’t know that if that is true, it is deliberate to deny them appeal. Because if the judge goes to London or Europe or anywhere outside the country, the records of proceedings from his judgment cannot be signed by any judge. “So no appeal could be had until he’s back. They didn’t know that they are playing on their intelligence, and that’s why Nigerian politicians are lazy. They don’t think,” Vanguard News The post ‘It’s unfortunate’ – Melaye reacts to Galadima’s claim on Justice Lifu’s illness appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: RFK Jr. Failed America on Measles
items.description: Measles is undeniably back. The disease, which was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, is once again endemic, the Pan American Health Organization reportedly decided at a meeting this week. PAHO made that determination based on a set of technical standards, and its official declaration is expected early next week. Those criteria say that measles is endemic when the same strain of the virus causes continuous infections for a year straight; even before this week’s meeting, publicly available data indicated that this was likely the case. But really, the evidence has been clear for some time now: The U.S. is in the midst of a measles crisis unlike any it’s faced in decades. More than 5,000 cases in 45 states have been confirmed this year. Pennsylvania started reporting measles deaths this August; its count is now up to seven. New York has had one death. Wisconsin reported its second yesterday. This is already America’s worst year for measles since 1991, which marked the end of a three-year epidemic in which 123 people died. That surge helped spur a national vaccination push. This time, the outbreak has unfolded on the watch of a health secretary who has declined to accept responsibility for its ongoing spread. Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has dismissed Democrats’ attempts to blame him for measles’ return. In April, he told a Senate committee that “the measles epidemic began before I came into office.” That’s true: Measles had already begun to spread in West Texas by January 2025, before Kennedy became health secretary. And routine childhood-vaccination rates, including the measles immunization, have declined since the coronavirus pandemic, which disrupted doctor appointments around the country. The U.S. isn’t alone in seeing cases rise. In January, six other countries—including Austria, Spain, and the United Kingdom—lost their elimination status. Measles was declared endemic in Canada again last year. But this is Kennedy’s crisis now. He’s been the nation’s top public-health official for nearly two years, and the country’s predicament has only deepened under his leadership. The number of measles cases in the U.S. in the first 10 months of the year is more than double the total for 2025. Meanwhile, Kennedy and the Department of Health and Human Services have failed to send a clear message to Americans about the importance of curbing the virus’s spread. As one CDC official, whose name I’m withholding to protect them from professional repercussions, recently told me, “The response has lacked a clear strategy and support from the top.” Kennedy’s CDC has offered help to states dealing with outbreaks. Recently, it’s sent staff to Pennsylvania, New York, and Wisconsin to assist with tasks such as contact tracing and surveillance. (In an emailed statement earlier this week, an HHS spokesperson cited that assistance and $100 million the CDC recently sent to states as evidence of the department’s “aggressive” response to measles.) But under Kennedy, the CDC’s response has also at times appeared constrained. The Washington Post reported that an alert that CDC scientists wanted to send regarding the risks of measles during pregnancy was not approved for unclear reasons. Meanwhile, at least some of the assistance the CDC has offered hasn’t been welcome. As Nicholas Florko reported in The Atlantic last year, Kennedy planned to send vitamin A to Texas, but health officials in the state had never requested any. (Vitamin A can help treat measles in children who have a severe deficiency but has not been shown to be effective for most Americans.) Perhaps most dramatically, Kennedy and his HHS have fought with states over the precise toll that measles has taken. In August, after two infants died in Pennsylvania, Kennedy and Governor Josh Shapiro got into a public dispute over whether measles contributed to those children’s deaths. As the number of deaths reported by states has continued to rise, the CDC has so far declined to attribute some of them to measles; its dashboard currently lists only six fatalities. Kennedy doesn’t talk about measles often. When he does, he tends to offer a tepid endorsement of the vaccine or downplay the seriousness of the disease. In 2024, during his failed presidential run, Kennedy—a longtime anti-vaccine activist—told an interviewer that he wouldn’t give his children the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine if they were born today. (Last year, he said he would “probably” do so.) He also claimed at the time that “kids who get the measles as a child are much healthier when they grow up,” which is not true. Last year, during an outbreak in Texas in which two young girls died, he offered only half-hearted support for vaccination while pushing vitamin A. As I reported at the time , Kennedy privately told the father of one young girl who had died of measles, “You don’t know what’s in the vaccine anymore.” This August, in the midst of a rapidly growing outbreak in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, Kennedy said on CNN that “parents should get their children vaccinated for measles”—but only after the host, Dana Bash, asked him to encourage parents to vaccinate their children. (The HHS spokesperson wrote that Kennedy and CDC Director Erica Schwartz “continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles.”) Such a statement would be entirely unremarkable for any previous health secretary, but it felt notable coming from Kennedy. Since that CNN interview, Kennedy has devoted few words to measles and far more to mocking Shapiro and promoting other projects, such as his cooking show. One recent episode explored how to make a chickpea salad. Kennedy has also kept mum on the many false statements about measles and vaccination from his allies and supporters. The anti-vaccine nonprofit Kennedy founded, Children’s Health Defense, published an article in September saying that “parents don’t need to be afraid of the measles” and asserting incorrectly that the virus can make children stronger. A week later, after four people had died in Pennsylvania, Kennedy told attendees at a Children’s Health Defense conference, “You have a strong and steadfast friend at the White House.” None of this reflects well on the health secretary, but he has shown no sign that he’ll change course. (HHS did not immediately respond this morning to a request for comment on PAHO’s reported decision.) President Trump has been supportive of Kennedy’s vaccine agenda, and combatting measles was never a focus of Kennedy’s Make America Healthy Again movement. In recent months, that movement has seemed to fray: One of the health secretary’s closest allies, Calley Means, quit his White House post in late October and then went on Joe Rogan’s podcast to complain about the influence of industry lobbyists in the federal government. The much-ballyhooed boost that MAHA would supposedly give Republicans in the midterms never materialized, either. Two of the movement’s most prominent candidates—Ken Paxton, the Senate nominee from Texas, and Zach Lahn, a candidate for governor in Iowa—lost their races by wide margins. But MAHA, and Kennedy, may not be chastened. The new White House chief of staff, Stephen Miller, appears to be anti-vaccine curious. He has echoed President Trump’s call to split the MMR into separate shots; the vaccines are not currently available separately, and experts say splitting them up is unnecessary. And he’s complained, without citing any particular evidence, that pressure to “pump your kids full of shots days after birth” is a “medical travesty.” (The White House declined to comment on Miller’s vaccine beliefs.) Kennedy cheered Miller’s promotion and wrote on X that it was time to “unleash the Kraken.” What, exactly, he means by that is unclear. But a disease that’s arguably the most contagious in history has already been unleashed on the United States, and Kennedy hasn’t shown nearly enough interest in reining it in.

items.title: Obi visits Oritsejafor, Uduaghan’s family in Delta
items.description: …meets traders, attends Catholic Charismatic Renewal Conference Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Labour Party in the 2023 general election, has visited former President of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Pastor Ayo Oritsejafor, and the family of the late former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan. Obi disclosed this in a statement on his X platform on Saturday, recounting his engagements in Delta State on Friday, November 13, 2026. He said he travelled to Warri after holding a town hall meeting in Lagos State the previous day, where he visited Oritsejafor, founder and Senior Pastor of Word of Life Bible Church, to celebrate his birthday. Obi congratulated the cleric and prayed for more productive years in God’s service. He subsequently visited the family of Uduaghan to offer his condolences over the former governor’s death. Obi described Uduaghan’s death as a painful personal loss, recalling the relationship they maintained while serving as governors of neighbouring states. He prayed for the peaceful repose of the deceased and strength for his family and others mourning him. The former Anambra State governor also disclosed that he briefly stopped at Ughelli Market while travelling by road from Warri to Asaba, where he interacted with traders and listened to their concerns about prevailing economic difficulties and challenges affecting their businesses. He said he assured the traders of his commitment to policies that would reduce the cost of living, strengthen small businesses and lift Nigerians out of poverty. Obi said he rounded off his engagements with a visit to the Catholic Charismatic Renewal Conference in Ubulu-Uku, where he urged worshippers to continue praying for public office holders to ensure that public resources were used for the benefit of citizens. He also reaffirmed his commitment, alongside his political ally, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, to national unity, tackling insecurity and corruption, and investing in critical sectors, particularly healthcare and education. Other priorities he highlighted included supporting small businesses and addressing poverty. Obi commended the party’s candidates in Delta State, led by its governorship candidate, Deacon Chris Iyovwaye, and senatorial candidate, Hon. Victor Ochei, for their participation and commitment. He also appreciated residents of the state for their hospitality. “A New Nigeria is Possible, and Nigeria will be OK,” he added. The post Obi visits Oritsejafor, Uduaghan’s family in Delta appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: FG raises alarm over 2,000 universities, 100 fake professors report
items.description: By Joseph Erunke, ABUJA The Federal Government has dismissed viral claims that Nigeria has 2,000 universities and that about 100 professors in the country were exposed as fake, describing the reports as fabricated misinformation aimed at eroding public confidence in the nation’s university system. The government, through the Federal Ministry of Education, said the National Universities Commission, NUC, never made such declarations, published the alleged list of fake professors or authenticated the names currently circulating on social media. Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, made the clarification in a statement issued on Saturday through the ministry’s Director of Press and Public Relations, Boriowo Folasade. He said the claims were false, misleading and a recycled version of old information being distorted to deceive the public. The ministry specifically faulted reports suggesting that the NUC had identified about 100 individuals as fake professors, explaining that the allegation was a misrepresentation of a media report published on December 3, 2019. According to the ministry, the original report concerned an exercise by the NUC to verify the directory of full professors in Nigerian universities and did not contain the names now being circulated online. It stressed that the commission had since disowned the purported list, insisting that it neither originated from the regulatory agency nor enjoyed its endorsement. 2,000 varsities On the claim that Nigeria has 2,000 universities, the ministry said the NUC had never announced the existence of such a number of universities in the country. The government expressed concern over what it described as the persistent recycling of false information, warning that such claims could undermine the credibility of Nigerian universities and damage efforts to strengthen standards in the nation’s higher education system. It urged media organisations, social media users and members of the public to exercise caution before sharing unverified information, particularly on issues concerning the recognition of universities and the integrity of academic qualifications. The ministry advised Nigerians to rely on the NUC’s official communication channels for accurate information on recognised universities, academic standards and regulatory decisions. It reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to supporting the NUC in protecting academic integrity, strengthening quality assurance and preserving the credibility and international reputation of Nigeria’s university education system. Vanguard News The post FG raises alarm over 2,000 universities, 100 fake professors report appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘Operation Feed Yourself’ cut Ghana’s rice imports to zero in 1975 and 1976 – Sam Jonah
items.description: Chancellor of the University of Cape Coast, Sir Sam Jonah, has credited the late General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong’s ‘Operation Feed Yourself’ with ending Ghana’s rice imports in 1975 and 1976. Speaking at the second edition of a lecture honouring the legacy of the former military leader on Friday, November 13, 2026 said the programme showed what national leadership can do when it gets citizens producing the food the country eats. Sir Sam said the idea began with a question Acheampong put to his government while reviewing its first budget. “Don’t we have the land? Don’t we have the rain? Don’t we have the water bodies? What is wrong with us?” Sir Sam Jonah quoted Acheampong asking why Ghana was buying rice abroad. The campaign was led by then Colonel Frank Bernasko, with chiefs and communities across the country taking part. The government sold cutlasses, hoes, fertiliser and seeds at heavily subsidised prices and also built irrigation dams to support production. According to Sir Sam, farmers in northern Ghana began exporting rice and tomatoes to neighbouring Upper Volta, now Burkina Faso, and Tamale picked up the nickname “Rice City.” He said the effect went beyond harvests as secondary schools grew their own food, university students volunteered to harvest sugar cane, and factory workers and bank managers farmed at weekends. In his words, it may have been the only time the educated Ghanaian was proud to call himself a farmer. Sir Sam argued that a country’s ability to feed itself is central to its development. He called Operation Feed Yourself a lasting part of Acheampong’s legacy and noted that successive governments have promised to revive it. In the remarks that formed part of a wider assessment of Acheampong’s record, Sir Sam made clear that recognising the former military leader’s policies does not mean endorsing the 1972 coup that brought him to power.

Seyi Tinubu denies viral quote on father’s tenure
items.description: …reports alleged fabrication to police, security agencies By Olasunkanmi Akoni Seyi Tinubu, son of President Bola Tinubu, has denied a viral statement circulating on social media claiming that nothing, including God, could stop his father from completing an eight-year tenure as President. Tinubu described the statement, which appeared on a social media poster allegedly circulated by supporters of Labour Party presidential candidate in the 2023 election, Peter Obi, as a fabrication intended to damage his reputation and provoke public outrage against his father. In a statement, he said he never made the comment attributed to him, describing it as an attempt at character assassination. “Let me state categorically and unequivocally: I never made such a statement,” he said. He disclosed that he had formally reported the alleged fabrication to the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant security agencies. According to him, investigations are underway to identify those responsible for creating and circulating the poster, adding that he would pursue legal action against those found culpable. Addressing the religious implications of the purported statement, Tinubu said his father’s presidency was achieved by the grace of Almighty God, stressing that only God determines the affairs of humanity. He described the attribution as offensive to his personal faith, arguing that no individual could challenge divine authority. The President’s son also called for an end to what he described as the politics of bitterness, misinformation, propaganda and deliberate character assassination. He warned against the use of social media anonymity to spread false information and damage people’s reputations for political purposes. The post Seyi Tinubu denies viral quote on father’s tenure appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mayweather plans boxing academies across Nigeria
items.description: …targets Africa’s next champions, eyes solid minerals investment By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA — Boxing legend and former world champion, Floyd Mayweather Jr., has announced plans to establish boxing academies across Nigeria to identify, nurture and develop young talents capable of competing on the international stage. Mayweather, who spoke during a visit to Nigeria on Friday, said the initiative would also involve organising boxing events across the country to provide emerging fighters with opportunities to showcase their abilities and build professional careers. He said Africa had enormous untapped sporting potential, adding that he was committed to supporting young people on the continent and giving back beyond his achievements in boxing. “My mission is always to be able to touch the people of Africa. I mean, Africa is the best continent in the world. And it’s always good to come back and receive the love from our people, to be able to touch the people, to let them know that if Floyd Mayweather did it, you guys can do it too,” he said. On plans to organise boxing events to discover young talents, Mayweather said the continent had abundant resources and talented people who deserved opportunities to excel. “Just the continent of Africa has so much talent. Africa has all the best resources in the world. And the music is amazing. The people are amazing. “It’s so beautiful to just come back here and be embraced by my people. So we look forward to coming over here, doing some fights, looking for talent over in Africa,” he added. Providing details of the initiative, the Consultant, TMT Africa, Dr Adrian Ogun, said Mayweather had fulfilled a promise made during his previous visit to Abuja in 2022 to return to Nigeria and promote boxing among young people. Ogun said the proposed programme, involving TMT Africa and Front Row Fight Series, led by its Chief Executive Officer, Keane Anis, would commence with a series of boxing events in early 2027. He explained that the initiative would extend beyond Abuja and Lagos to other cities, including Enugu and Calabar. According to him, the programme would establish boxing academies and provide technical expertise and equipment to identify and develop young fighters. Ogun lamented that many Nigerian boxers had been forced to travel abroad to access the facilities, training and opportunities required to advance their careers. “We have suffered from a problem where all of our boxers have gone abroad to develop themselves. Those that were able to get that opportunity,” he said. He cited Nigerian heavyweight boxer Efe Ajagba as an example of a fighter who had to pursue his professional development outside the country. Ogun said the initiative would also create opportunities for Nigerian boxers to gain international exposure through partnerships with established boxing facilities abroad. He proposed a partnership between Nigerian boxing academies and Mayweather’s gym in Las Vegas, United States, to improve training standards and expose young fighters to international coaching expertise. He further disclosed that Mayweather had expressed interest in investing in Nigeria’s solid minerals sector, indicating that the boxer’s interest in the country extended beyond sports. Speaking on the proposed investment, Mayweather said his interest in Africa was not limited to financial returns but also involved ensuring that Africans benefited from their natural resources. “It’s not just about making money in Africa. It’s about making money all around the world, but also giving back to the people. “Telling the people that you guys should own your resources. You guys should keep your resources in-house,” he said. On whether he would stage a boxing bout in Nigeria, Ogun said he believed Mayweather was interested in returning to organise an event in the country, although details were yet to be finalised. He added that the Nigerian Boxing Board of Control (NBBoC) was supportive of efforts to revitalise the sport, disclosing that he had met with the organisation as part of moves to establish collaboration. Meanwhile, Mayweather is scheduled to face Australian light heavyweight boxer Matt “The Jedi” Floyd in an exhibition bout in Bangkok, Thailand, on December 19, 2026. The boxing legend urged African youths to remain focused, work hard and believe in their abilities. “My message to the African youth, keep believing. Keep working hard. Know you guys are number one. Africa, know you guys are number one,” he said. The post Mayweather plans boxing academies across Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .
