items.title: La Bulgarie ne livrera plus d’armes à l’Ukraine puisées dans les stocks de son armée
items.description: La Bulgarie refuse de nouveaux engagements financiers pour l'armement de Kiev. Le 13 novembre, a Dublin, le Premier ministre Roumen Radev a rappele que son pays ne pouvait pas contribuer a une nouvelle enveloppe militaire europeenne. Sofia, vise par une procedure pour deficit excessif, invoque l'etat de ses finances publiques. Le dirigeant bulgare a aussi reaffirme une decision annoncee des l'arrivee de son gouvernement : « Notre position est claire : nous ne fournirons desormais plus d'armes ni de munitions des stocks de l'armee bulgare. » Le meme jour, Donald Tusk, Premier ministre polonais, a ferme une autre porte a Kiev. Il a annonce qu'il ne debloquerait pas d'argent supplementaire pour le programme PURL de l'OTAN, destine a acheter aux etats-Unis des armes pour l'Ukraine. La Pologne continue d'apporter d'autres formes de soutien, mais ne veut plus contribuer a ce mecanisme. La Hongrie, la Slovaquie et la Tchequie ne veulent pas participer a une nouvelle dette commune. Friedrich Merz exige au contraire que les etats membres prennent tous leur part. Le chancelier allemand a lie le financement ukrainien aux discussions sur le prochain budget europeen . Le Premier ministre slovaque Robert Fico a denonce cette pression : « Aujourd'hui, nous devons reagir face a ce chantage. [...] Ce que fait le chancelier allemand releve du chantage pur et simple, et je m'y oppose. » La facture ne cesse de grossir pour l'UE Les Europeens ont pourtant deja approuve un emprunt de 90 milliards d'euros pour l'Ukraine en 2026 et 2027. Sur cette somme, 24,1 milliards ont ete verses, selon le Conseil de l'UE. Mais le 16 octobre, Volodymyr Zelensky a reclame 70 milliards d'euros supplementaires pour 2027 , au-dela des financements prevus. En septembre, Kiev sollicitait deja 27 milliards de dollars de financement additionnel pour l'annee en cours, tout en reclamant l'acceleration de versements europeens. Le 5 novembre, Zelensky revenait sur les 70 milliards esperes pour 2027, assurant avoir recu un accueil favorable a Bruxelles. En France, Marine Le Pen a resume les tensions le 13 novembre sur X : « Le financement de l'Ukraine secoue aujourd'hui l'Europe : 90 milliards d'emprunts ont deja ete effectues et plusieurs pays s'opposent a un financement supplementaire. » Le financement de l’Ukraine secoue aujourd’hui l’Europe : 90 milliards d’emprunts ont déjà été effectués et plusieurs pays s’opposent à un financement supplémentaire. Si je peux rencontrer Volodymyr Zelensky à Bruxelles, il sera intéressant d’en discuter. https://t.co/B9Jpxy5hwC — Marine Le Pen (@MLP_officiel) November 13, 2026

items.title: Achraf Hakimi, le « meilleur latéral du monde » selon AS
items.description: Le quotidien sportif espagnol AS n’a pas tari d’éloges sur Achraf Hakimi après la large victoire du Maroc face au Niger (5-1), vendredi soir, en éliminatoires de la CAN. Le journal madrilène voit dans l’international marocain le « meilleur latéral du monde », soulignant son influence majeure dans le succès des Lions de l’Atlas. Dans un article intitulé « Il n’y en a pas d’autre comme Achraf », AS met en avant la prestation XXL du défenseur du Paris Saint-Germain, auteur de deux buts et d’une passe décisive face au Niger. « Achraf est celui qui commande » , écrit le quotidien espagnol, estimant que le Maroc « danse à son rythme depuis un bon moment déjà ». Pour AS, le latéral marocain confirme une nouvelle fois son statut au plus haut niveau, aussi bien par son impact offensif que par sa capacité à peser sur le jeu. Le journal revient notamment sur les deux réalisations de Hakimi, mettant en avant la qualité de sa frappe depuis l’extérieur de la surface, venue se loger dans la lucarne opposée, avant de souligner la précision de son coup franc, exécuté à la perfection. « Il n’y a pas d’autre latéral comme lui aujourd’hui dans le monde » , conclut AS, visiblement impressionné par la prestation du capitaine marocain. Une attaque aux accents de Liga Le quotidien espagnol s’est également attardé sur les qualités offensives des Lions de l’Atlas. AS décrit une attaque aux « accents de Liga espagnole », portée notamment par Brahim Diaz, Abde et Yassir Zabiri. Le journal associe ainsi Brahim Diaz à la « classe du Real Madrid », Abde au « tranchant du Real Betis » et Zabiri à la « foi inépuisable du Racing de Santander », mettant en avant la diversité des profils offensifs à disposition de Mohamed Ouahbi. La rencontre a également été marquée par un moment symbolique pour Yassine Bounou, honoré avant le coup d’envoi pour sa 100e sélection avec l’équipe nationale marocaine. Avec cette victoire convaincante, le Maroc consolide sa première place du groupe A avec neuf points et se rapproche de la qualification pour la prochaine Coupe d’Afrique des Nations. Pour AS, cette dynamique confirme surtout la montée en puissance d’une sélection marocaine portée par des individualités de premier plan, au premier rang desquelles figure désormais, une nouvelle fois, Achraf Hakimi. The post Achraf Hakimi, le « meilleur latéral du monde » selon AS appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Elias Zerhouni officiellement nommé président du Conseil scientifique de la diaspora algérienne
items.description: Sans surprise, le professeur Elias Zerhouni est nommé président du Haut conseil de la communauté algérienne à l'étranger , sur décision du président de la République Abdelmadjid Tebboune. Le décret portant nomination du radiologue et professeur de médecine algéro-américain vient d'être publié au Journal officiel. Diaspora algérienne : Elias Zerhouni désigné sans surprise à la tête du Haut conseil scientifique Le Haut conseil scientifique de la diaspora algérienne est un organisme nouvellement créé à l’initiative du chef de l'Etat avec comme objectif de permettre aux compétences algériennes expatriées de contribuer à l'effort de développement du pays. Le conseil a tenu sa réunion constitutive en juin dernier à Alger, avec déjà le professeur Zerhouni comme coordinateur. Le décret fixant les missions et l’organisation du conseil a été publié le 7 septembre, stipulant que parmi les missions qui lui sont assignées, celle de contribuer au renforcement de la participation des compétences scientifiques expatriées et de proposer “des mécanismes durables pour les relier au système national d'enseignement supérieur, de recherche scientifique et d'innovation, afin de développer le capital humain et assurer le développement économique, social, scientifique, technique et culturel du pays”. Zerhouni : “L’idée est de faire quelque chose ensemble pour le pays” Ses membres, au nombre de 39, ont été reçus fin septembre par le président Tebboune. Y figurent des éminences de la recherche scientifique en Amérique et en Europe, dont Elias Zerhouni, Yasmine Belkaid, Belkacem Haba, Karim Zaghib, Noureddine Melikechi… “Actuellement en Algérie, nous avons toutes les capacités, il y a des jeunes qui se distinguent dans des compétitions internationales. L’idée est de faire quelque chose ensemble pour le pays, nous qui connaissons l'étranger et ceux qui connaissent l’intérieur du pays”, a déclaré Zerhouni à l'issue de l’audience. Elias Zerhouni, un éminent professeur reconnu aux États-Unis Elias Zerhouni est nommé président du conseil en vertu d’un décret présidentiel daté du 4 novembre 2026, publié dans le dernier numéro du Journal officiel. “M. Adam Elias Zerhouni est nommé président du haut conseil de la communauté scientifique nationale à l'étranger”, y lit-on. Né à Nedroma (Tlemcen) en 1951, Elias Zerhouni a fait l'essentiel de sa carrière de médecin et de professeur de médecine aux États-Unis, notamment à la faculté de médecine de l'Université Johns Hopkins. Entre 2002 et 2008, il a occupé le poste prestigieux de directeur des National Institutes of Health (NIH). L'éminent radiologue avait été nommé par Georges W. Bush, alors président des États-Unis. L’article Elias Zerhouni officiellement nommé président du Conseil scientifique de la diaspora algérienne est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Opposition sponsored Tinubu’s booing to portray Wike as failure – FCT coalition
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Coalition of Youth Civil Society Groups in the Federal Capital Territory FCT has alleged that opposition political interests sponsored the booing of President Bola Tinubu at a mosque in Abuja in order to portray the FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, as one who cannot keep his promises. The coalition’s coordinator, Ifeoma Adegbe, made the allegation on Saturday in a statement. “Let me make it clear: we condemn this act, which we believe was sponsored by the opposition simply to have something to circulate on social media. Their intention is to use such incidents to deceive Nigerians, manipulate public opinion and gain cheap popularity by discrediting the good work of President Tinubu through the Honourable Minister of the FCT. “They want to create the impression in the public domain that the FCT Minister cannot keep his promises and has done nothing for the territory. We reject that narrative. We say no to this attempt to mislead the public, and we condemn the sponsorship of any group to manufacture political disturbances in our territory,” Adegbe said. The coordinator was reacting to events at the Shehu Shagari Central Mosque in Abuja on Friday, November 13, where some worshippers and youths reportedly booed the President, chanting “Tinubu Must Go”, “Ba ma so” and “Ba ma yi” as his convoy departed the premises. Videos of the incident circulated widely on social media, with reports claiming that some individuals threw stones and other objects towards the presidential convoy. The Presidency, however, disputed aspects of the reports. The President’s Senior Special Assistant on Digital Engagement, Strategy and New Media, O’tega Ogra, released a video showing Tinubu leaving amid greetings from some supporters. Adegbe alleged that some of those who booed the President and chanted anti-government slogans were brought into the territory from other states after news of his planned visit. “We condemn this act in its entirety. We are inhabitants of the FCT and genuine residents of this territory. We have information that these individuals were brought in from different states after learning that Mr President would be observing Friday prayers at the mosque. They were sponsored, and we strongly condemn such political manipulation,” Adegbe said. Adegbe argued that the alleged sponsorship of protesters was part of a wider effort to undermine the relationship between the FCT administration and residents by discrediting government interventions. Adegbe maintained that political disagreements should not be exploited to misrepresent the interests of indigenous communities, stressing that the right of residents to express their opinions must be respected. The coalition also urged political parties and their supporters to avoid actions capable of escalating tensions as preparations gather momentum for the 2027 general elections, and called on residents to distinguish between genuine public grievances and allegations of orchestrated political activities. The coordinator said the coalition would not allow individuals allegedly imported from outside the territory to speak for its indigenous communities, and that the reported protest would not alter its political commitment. “We know the genuine voters of the FCT, and we know the position of our people. We have promised and vowed that we must deliver 65 per cent of our votes in the FCT to President Bola Tinubu. Nobody should mistake the activities of a group of individuals for the collective decision of our people,” Adegbe stated. The post Opposition sponsored Tinubu’s booing to portray Wike as failure – FCT coalition appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Keyamo gives Dickson 48 hours to clarify NDC’s anthem position
items.description: Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, has challenged Senator Seriake Dickson, national leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), to clarify whether the party officially endorses the singing of a proscribed national anthem. Keyamo, in a post on his X platform on Saturday, gave Dickson 48 hours to state the party’s position on the matter. The minister described the national anthem as one of a country’s national symbols, representing its history, values and sovereignty. He argued that the national anthem was intended to unite citizens, warning that deliberately singing a different anthem from the one prescribed by law could raise concerns about national unity and sovereignty. READ ALSO: Obi leads NDC supporters in singing old national anthem in Lagos According to Keyamo, when a group of people chooses to sing an alternative anthem in defiance of the one prescribed by law, it could be interpreted as laying the groundwork for secession. He further argued that when the leader of such a group endorses the action, it could amount to the group officially adopting a secessionist position. Addressing Dickson directly, Keyamo described him as his former classmate and friend, recalling their school days and commending his courage. He said: “I AM THEREFORE OFFICIALLY CALLING ON the original ‘COUNTRYMAN’, my CLASSMATE, my friend and a man of considerable courage from our school days, SENATOR SERIAKE DICKSON, the official leader of the NDC, to within 48 hours SPEAK UP as to whether the NDC officially endorses a proscribed anthem as its own NATIONAL SYMBOL. The world is waiting.” Keyamo’s challenge places the NDC leadership under pressure to clarify its position on the alleged adoption or endorsement of an alternative national anthem. items.title: ‘IDPs will return home’ – Tinubu promises Plateau security
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – President Bola Tinubu has assured residents of Plateau State that his administration will rebuild communities attacked by gunmen and ensure the return of internally displaced persons, IDPs, to their ancestral homes. Read Also: 2027: Why Tinubu may still win presidential election Tinubu gave the assurance on Saturday while speaking at the APC North-Central Presidential Campaign Rally at the Zaria Road Stadium, Jos. Also, he promised to strengthen security operations across the state and other parts of the country. He said: “I got the report from the governor, and I saw hope in the faces of our people. It is now that we can rebuild, and I assure those displaced that we will rebuild your communities and bring you back to your communities. “I have directed all the security agencies to take decisive action. What we should be getting is stability and prosperity, not crisis. “Our government was not elected to inflict wounds on one another or to bury people. We have to lift people up from penury to prosperity.” The President disclosed that his administration was reinforcing security deployment and strengthening coordination among security agencies to improve rapid response to security threats. “We are reinforcing security deployment and strengthening coordination and rapid response. One thousand forest guards are undergoing training right now. “You will feel them, you will see them, and you will feel secure in your villages and communities. “The surveillance cameras have already been procured, as I promised. They will further strengthen early detection and early warning security operations,” he said. Tinubu reiterated his commitment to addressing the plight of displaced persons, saying the Federal Government would work with the Plateau State Government and community leaders to facilitate their resettlement. “To our displaced families, I say once again that government is working to end your suffering and bring you back to rebuild your communities. “We will work with the governor, traditional rulers and other leaders to rebuild those communities and take you back to settle in the comfort of where you belong,” he said. The President commended the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr Bernard Doro, for his contributions to supporting vulnerable Nigerians and displaced persons. “I appreciate the contribution of your son, Dr Bernard Doro, Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, to this important responsibility.” “Doro is doing a very good job identifying the vulnerable and the neediest and stretching the hand of humanity to them,” he said. Tinubu urged residents of Plateau State to embrace peaceful coexistence, saying the future of the state depended on unity, mutual respect and understanding among its people. “The future on this land is shared. Living together peacefully is a necessity we must nurture with patience, fairness and mutual respect. “I plead with you to forget whatever differences we may have. Let us work together for one country,” he said. The President also urged eligible voters to obtain and use their Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs, to support the APC in the forthcoming elections. “Do you have your voter’s registration card? That is your weapon. That is your roadmap to prosperity. Use it effectively to vote for the APC,” he told the crowd. He assured residents that the 2027 elections would be peaceful, urging them not to be intimidated by individuals seeking to cause violence. … on economy Tinubu further promised to support the development of Plateau’s economy through improved transportation and agricultural exports, including plans to convert the state’s airport into a cargo airport. “We are going to convert your airport into a cargo airport. From there, you will be able to ship vegetables and potatoes abroad directly. The economy will improve, and prosperity will grow,” he said. Meanwhile, Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who also addressed the rally, praised Tinubu for taking what he described as courageous economic decisions that saved Nigeria from economic collapse. Shettima said, “We were on the verge of collapse. We were on the road to Caracas, but our President had the courage and conviction to take far-reaching decisions that have saved the economy from collapse. “He is indeed a transformational leader, and I believe posterity will be kind to him. Now our economy is on a sound footing. Our foreign reserves are hovering in the neighbourhood of $60 billion.” The Vice-President said he particularly admired Tinubu for accepting responsibility for the country’s economic situation instead of blaming his predecessor, former President Muhammadu Buhari. “Most importantly, I respect him fundamentally for one thing. A lot of leaders, upon assuming the mantle of leadership, have two options: either to continue to kick the ball down the alley or blame their predecessors.” “But President Tinubu assumed the mantle of leadership and, according to him, he had to take over the assets and liabilities of his predecessor,” he said. Shettima also described Plateau as a gift to Nigeria, citing the contributions of prominent leaders from the state to national development. “To the good people of Plateau State, you are a gift to the nation. Plateau has given this nation great leaders such as John Kadiya, John Shagaya, Jeremiah Useni, and Solomon Lar. He urged the people to support Tinubu and Governor Caleb Mutfwang in the 2027 elections, saying the political differences that divided APC leaders in the state during the 2023 elections had been resolved. “I urge you, I beseech you, I implore you, on January 16 next year, to rally around our great leader. I want you to vote for our President. I want you to vote for our governor,” Shettima said. items.title: What a New Congress Could Mean For Hegseth
items.description: Editor's Note: Washington Week With The Atlantic is a partnership between NewsHour Productions, WETA, and The Atlantic airing every Friday on PBS stations nationwide. Check your local listings , watch full episodes here , or listen to the weekly podcast here . Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth avoided an impeachment vote in the House, but Democrats could launch a new effort when they take control of Congress. On Washington Week With The Atlantic , panelists joined to discuss this and more. “We have to remember that we’re a nation at war,” Michele Norris, a senior contributing editor at MS NOW, argued last night. “Normally, when a country is at war, you’re trying to build a case for what you’re doing; you’re trying to bring along the American public.” What Hegseth is facing is “a larger problem than just impeachment,” she added. Joining the editor in chief of The Atlantic , Jeffrey Goldberg, to discuss this and more: John Dickerson, a contributing writer at The Atlantic ; Jonathan Karl, a chief Washington correspondent at ABC News; and Norris. items.title: Pakistan to host 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting on Nov 15-16
items.description: The 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers will be held in Islamabad on Nov 15 and 16, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Saturday. The meeting will be chaired by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and attended by foreign ministers and heads of delegations from ECO member states, along with representatives of the organisation’s secretariat and subsidiary bodies, the FO said in a statement. The ministerial meeting will be preceded by a meeting of senior officials of ECO member states, which will review the organisation’s activities and programmes, assess the work of its subsidiary bodies and finalise the agenda and draft outcome documents for consideration by the ministers. Pakistan, which holds the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27, will seek to advance the organisation’s objectives under the theme “Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO”, the FO said. It said Pakistan’s chairmanship would focus on strengthening regional connectivity and integration, deepening partnerships and promoting collective efforts for economic prosperity and sustainable development. The chairmanship would also provide an opportunity to strengthen the ECO’s role as a platform for regional cooperation, dialogue and economic collaboration, it added. According to the FO, Pakistan also aims to position itself as a regional connectivity hub, facilitate logistics supply chains and help shape the agenda for regional trade. The efforts would help unlock the region’s economic potential and translate the benefits of regional cooperation into tangible improvements in the lives of people in ECO member states, the statement said. In a post on X, Dar welcomed the delegates arriving for the meeting. “I look forward to productive deliberations as we work together to strengthen regional cooperation and advance our shared priorities. Wishing all delegates a productive and memorable stay in Islamabad,” he said. Meanwhile, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus Tahsin Ertuğruloğlu arrived in Islamabad to participate in the meeting. He was received at the airport by officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Last month, DPM Dar directed relevant authorities to ensure flawless coordination and timely preparations for the ECO meeting, underscoring the deep importance Pakistan attaches to the regional bloc. The 17th ECO Summit was held in Azerbaijan’s Khankendi on July 3-4, 2025, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif leading Pakistan’s delegation. The summit brought together heads of state and government from member countries to discuss regional cooperation and economic integration. During the summit, Pakistan called for enhanced intra-regional trade, transport connectivity, energy cooperation and sustainable development, while reaffirming its commitment to the ECO Vision 2025.

items.title: Major among 4 troops martyred, 24 terrorists killed during operations in KP and Balochistan: ISPR
items.description: Four troops, including a major, were martyred while 24 terrorists were killed in multiple intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan, the military’s media wing said on Saturday. In a statement , Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that since Nov 13, armed forces have been conducting multiple IBOs “around Kolpur, Kardagap and Nushki, including area domination and patrolling of the Quetta-Taftan National Highway (N-40) to keep it secure for local traffic and sustain operations”. On the night of Nov 13/14 in Kolpur, security forces “successfully neutralised eight Indian-sponsored terrorists of Fitna al Hindustan ( FAH ), including a suicide bomber, and recovered a large cache of weapons and ammunition”, ISPR said. The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. It added that on Nov 14, FAH terrorists “targeted military vehicles on patrol with armed quadcopters”, resulting in the martyrdom of Major Omer Minhas Nasir, resident of Chakwal district, and Havildar Muhammad Adnan Khan from Kotli Sattian. “This cowardly act has not shaken the resolve of the security forces. The tempo of operations will be maintained and IBOs will continue with the same vigour to secure the local population and eliminate the menace of terrorism,” ISPR affirmed. It added that clearance operations in these areas will continue “until the threat is completely neutralised”. This photo, shared by ISPR on Nov 14, shows ammunition and equipment recovered from terrorists in Balochistan. It further said: “Backed by India and other hostile intelligence agencies, FAH is actively trying to use drones and other technical means, including IEDs (improvised explosive devices), to target innocent civilians and security forces, so as to undermine the efforts of the government and security forces to maintain peace and normalcy in the area.” Accusing India of providing terrorists full financial support and supplying it with the “latest gadgetry”, the ISPR asserted, “The security forces are fully alive to this evolving threat and will deny the terrorists any space, whatever means they employ.” ISPR affirmed that the “relentless counterterrorism campaign under vision ‘ Azm-i- Istehkam ’, as approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan , will continue at full pace”. The military’s media wing warned that security forces and law enforcement agencies “will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country”. In an earlier statement, ISPR said two soldiers were martyred and 16 terrorists were killed as security forces continued a series of IBOs in North Waziristan. According to the military’s media wing, multiple khwarij locations were engaged in the general areas of Mir Ali, Datta Khel and surrounding areas in North Waziristan. “Following fierce fire exchanges, in last twelve hours, 12 khwarij , including two Afghan nationals belonging to Indian-sponsored Fitna al Khwarij were sent to hell in Ali Khel, while two khwarij each were neutralised in Mir Ali and Datta Khel, thereby causing a significant blow to the khwarijs ’ network operating in the area,” ISPR said. Fitna al Khawarij is a term used by the state for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). ISPR said that during the operations, 43-year-old Havildar Asmat Ali and 32-year-old Naik Aftab Ali embraced martyrdom. “Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the killed Indian-sponsored khwarij , who remained actively involved in numerous terrorist activities, including the killing of innocent civilians,” it said. The statement said that sanitisation operations would continue to eliminate “remaining holed-up khwarij from these areas”, adding that the counterterrorism campaign would continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored terrorism from the country. ‘Step forward in war against terrorism’ President Asif Ali Zardari, in separate statements , paid tribute to the security forces for their successful operations and expressed condolences over the martyrdom of the troops. He expressed his condolences to the bereaved families of the martyrs, terming the sacrifices by officers and soldiers a “source of pride for the entire nation”. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif appreciated the professional competence, bravery and prompt action of the security forces. He commended the security forces for eliminating 16 terrorists “belonging to Fitna al-Khwarij, who were operating under Indian patronage” in North Waziristan, state-run APP quoted his office as saying. “The supreme sacrifices of our brave soldiers further strengthen our national resolve to completely eradicate terrorism,” he said and reiterated that operations against terrorism would continue until its complete elimination from the country. The prime minister resolved that the fight against “foreign-backed terrorism” would continue with full force, determination and steadfastness till its complete eradication. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said he was deeply saddened by the martyrdom of “brave military personnel in a drone attack on a military convoy in Kirdgap, Mastung”. Strongly condemning the “cowardly attack”, Dar affirmed that the nation “stands united with our armed forces and resolute in its determination to eliminate terrorism”. In his statement, Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti termed the killing of eight terrorists a “significant step forward in the war against terrorism”. In a post on X, he declared that “every attempt to spread unrest in Balochistan and block the path to development will be thwarted”. Paying tribute to the martyred major and havildar, CM Bugti wrote, “The state is committed to completely eradicating terrorism and protecting the lives and property of the people. There will be no compromise on peace and stability in Balochistan.” Rise in terrorism The operations come a day after ISPR said 74 terrorists were killed in IBOs in KP and Balochistan. On Friday, it said 43 terrorists were killed during operations conducted over 48 hours in KP, including 35 in North Waziristan’s Mir Ali and eight in Orakzai district. Another 31 terrorists were killed in Balochistan during an operation launched on Nov 3. Pakistan has seen a surge in terrorism, especially in KP and Balochistan, since the banned TTP ended its ceasefire deal with the government in November 2022, vowing to increase attacks. According to Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies , the country’s security environment continued to show considerable volatility from Oct 30 to Nov 5, 2026, with renewed terrorist activity in parts of KP and the former tribal districts, alongside intensified counterterrorism operations and changing patterns of militant violence. While attacks rose from 8 to 20 in former tribal districts, Balochistan presented a different pattern; it recorded 11 attacks, down from 15 the previous week, although fatalities increased from five to seven. The weekly increase came against the backdrop of a substantial month-on-month reduction in terrorist violence recorded during October . Earlier this month, a soldier was martyred and 17 terrorists were killed in two IBOs conducted in Balochistan’s Kachhi and Kharan districts on Nov 1, ISPR said. Correction: An earlier version of this story said 14 terrorists were killed in North Waziristan. The error is regretted.

items.title: Don’t Be So Surprised That Mississippi Turned Blue
items.description: Scott Colom, the first Black U.S. senator ever elected by Mississippians, traces his lineage in the state back seven generations, to when the nation was forging its foundation on the backs of stolen Black people. He waged a campaign set on showing that “Mississippi matters,” which many registered more as a question than a declaration, doubting whether a Black man and a Democrat could win the seat. During the most expensive election cycle in U.S. history, his campaign coffers were empty compared with Democrats in other battleground races. Finally victorious on Veterans Day, he credited the state’s civil-rights titans and local people who work without an expectation of recognition for carrying on the “Mississippi faith tradition” of having hope, even—or perhaps especially—in dark chapters. Many Americans might be surprised that Colom flipped what’s long been a deeply red seat. But this win is the product of decades of uphill, incremental, thankless, and overlooked labor powered by an ancestral charge and a conviction to reclaim Mississippi. My late stepfather, Obbie Riley, a five-term Democratic county supervisor in Mississippi, was among those who undertook that fight, although he didn’t live long enough to see its results. The state’s “faith tradition” that Colom evoked is as much about prayer as it is about remembering generations of bloodshed in Mississippi, where Black voting rights were redeemed by those who could only dream of what Colom has now achieved: finally turning his home state blue. “There were times when I was tired, and I felt like I couldn’t keep going, but I kept the faith,” Colom said during his victory speech Wednesday night. “And that is another tradition of our state. There’s so many people that had faith in Mississippi at times where it seemed impossible.” That faith, and the hard work that must accompany it, was something Colom learned in his household, where he and his twin brother were reared by now-retired Judge Dorothy Colom, the first Black person to be elected to her region’s chancery court, and Wilbur Colom, an attorney who was once a Republican. Scott built on this pedigree, attending the University of Wisconsin to study law and returning home to the Columbus area, in the east-central pocket of the state, not far from the Alabama line. There he became the youngest and the first African American justice-court judge in Lowndes County, in 2011, and then Columbus’s first African American city prosecutor, in 2013. Later he took a bolder step, campaigning for district attorney in his early 30s. [ Adam Serwer: Even where MAGA won, MAGA lost ] If Columbus were anywhere else, it might be described as a natural incubator for a Democratic U.S. senator. It is a college town, home to the state’s women’s university; it’s also a vertex of a region known as “The Golden Triangle,” which is anchored by Mississippi State University and an Air Force base in Starkville. Colom ran for district attorney in 2015 as a reform candidate—and unseated a 27-year incumbent who’d defended debunked medical-examiner analyses that had led to multiple false convictions that were later overturned. Colom has been the region’s top cop for more than a decade; he instituted restorative justice and counseling for gun-violence survivors, among other reforms. In 2020, days after George Floyd was murdered, Mississippi’s attorney general suddenly dropped a police-shooting case that Colom had transferred to the state in 2016. Colom was outspoken about it, making parts of the case file public and expressing regret for handing the case over. History is never fully in the rearview in Mississippi, and that was evident throughout the Colom campaign. On the day before he delivered his victory speech, at Tougaloo College, a historically Black school with a rich civil-rights history, Colom held a press conference wearing a mocha-brown hoodie that bore a quote from the civil-rights organizer Bob Moses: When you’re in Mississippi, the rest of America doesn’t seem real. And when you’re in the rest of America, Mississippi doesn’t seem real. Moses directed Freedom Summer, the 1964 effort to recruit hundreds of white college students to Mississippi to help open Freedom Schools, or voter-registration-and-education sites meant to overcome the ridicule, violence, and other tactics the state used to keep Black voters off the rolls. At the time, the state had the lowest Black voter-registration numbers, despite being the Blackest state in the U.S. Training for the college students was under way when members of the Ku Klux Klan burned down Mt. Zion United Methodist Church in Philadelphia, Mississippi, after beating parishioners suspected of holding civil-rights meetings. Michael Schwerner and James Chaney, organizers who had done grassroots work at Mt. Zion, knew they had to leave Freedom Summer training in Ohio to check on the community. Andrew Goodman, a college student who volunteered for Freedom Summer, joined them on his first trip to Mississippi. On the afternoon of June 21, as the trio made their way through the center of Philadelphia, the deputy sheriff, a Klansman, pulled them over and arrested them. When they were released after nightfall, a group of Klansmen and law enforcement kidnapped them, killed them, and buried them in an earthen dam in Neshoba County, where an FBI search located them 44 days later. This past summer, Colom made a campaign stop at the Neshoba County Fair, where politicians frequently stump. Ronald Reagan spoke there during his 1980 presidential campaign, emphasizing his belief in states’ rights, which many interpreted as a dog whistle, given the proximity to where the three civil-rights workers had been slain. Colom’s father worked for Reagan’s transition team. In a 1981 interview with The Daily Mississippian , the University of Mississippi’s student newspaper, Wilbur Colom criticized some of Reagan’s policies and said that the GOP of the ’50s and ’60s had been deficient in its support for civil-rights legislation, but that Black voters’ commitment to the Democratic Party shouldn’t be automatic either. Wilbur’s son ran a campaign with a complementary refrain: Why should Mississippi automatically be considered a Republican stronghold, especially when Democrats have chipped away at GOP control in statewide elections over the past decade? When my stepfather died in September, he was the lone Black person and Democrat serving as a Neshoba County supervisor. And although that set him apart, he’s remembered for how he sifted through disagreements to move forward, even if the ideological overlap with his colleagues was the size of a grain of sand. Throughout his campaign, Colom likewise touted that he would work with anyone, Republican or otherwise; he even visited a Trump rally and spoke with people waiting in line. There’s a Mississippi brand of bipartisanship, one my stepdad practiced, that’s a mainstay especially in rural areas, where people of difference have found commonality even amid bitter political and racial tensions. Colom’s win was propelled by grassroots organizing to register voters, get them to the polls, and, in some cases, help them return to certify or cure provisional ballots. The senator-elect outraised his opponent, the incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith, in the last quarter of the campaign ( approximately $1.45 million to $864,000), but that was nothing compared with the money pouring in for other Democratic Senate candidates. Colom’s campaign had a “rich message but a poor treasury,” Representative Bennie Thompson said at the Tougaloo victory party, where he introduced the senator-elect. With seemingly nothing to lose, Colom infused a little bit of fun into his campaign, producing a series of ads that showcased his sense of humor. One, called “Sinators,” parodied the Mississippi-based movie Sinners using Colom’s identical twin brother. In it, a Hyde-Smith look-alike asks for just one more chance to keep everything in Mississippi the way it is. Hyde-Smith, whose parents sent her to a segregation academy as a child, was caught on camera in 2018 saying of a supporter standing beside her that if he “invited me to a public hanging, I’d be on the front row”—in the state where more known lynchings occurred than in any other. (She later said that the remark was an “exaggerated expression of regard.”) She conceded the race after it was called on Wednesday, and congratulated Colom on his victory. The moment had a karmic quality: After President Biden nominated Colom to the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi in 2022, Hyde-Smith single-handedly blocked him from the lifetime appointment, even though other statewide Republicans supported him for the role. For a time, it looked as if the election results might face legal challenges. During the week-long vote counting, Hyde-Smith was asked about the possibility of fraud in the election and said, “There’s always irregularities .” In the summer of 2025, Mississippi shifted tens of thousands of voters to “inactive” status based on data from the credit-reporting agency Experian. DeSoto County, home to the white-flight suburbs of Memphis, inactivated more than 15,000 voters, more than anywhere else in the state . On Election Day, lines there lagged, and polling stations ran low on affidavit ballots. Colom won the county with about 53 percent of the vote; Hyde-Smith had won the county in her previous two elections. The first time the Department of Justice used the now-gutted 1965 Voting Rights Act to protect white voters happened in Colom’s district, in Noxubee County, in 2005; Wilbur Colom represented the defendant in the case . A decade later, around the time that Scott Colom was running for district attorney, a DOJ lawyer from the 2005 case filed a lawsuit alleging issues with the Noxubee voter rolls. Instead of undertaking a costly fight, the county entered a consent decree that required a period of scrutinized voter-roll management. Noxubee and Lowndes, another county in Colom’s district, also saw voter inactivations surge in the months before the 2026 midterms. This living history is another reason many doubted whether Colom, or any Black senatorial candidate, could make it to Washington. Political pundits have already compared this moment to the Barack Obama elections, which saw high Black voter turnout in Mississippi and elsewhere. Nadia Colom—the wife of the senator-elect, a real-estate agent, and former executive director of the Golden Triangle Boys and Girls Club—said in her speech on Wednesday that people have been calling her “Mississippi’s Michelle,” referring to the former first lady. “While it’s an honor, really and truly, to be seen in that light, what really means the most to me is that I get to be called Mississippi’s ,” she said. [ Read: Why Black voters abandoned Trump ] Colom’s campaign rightly touts him as the first Black U.S. senator to be elected by Mississippians. Mississippi sent two Black senators—Hiram Revels, the nation’s first Black senator, and later Blanche Bruce—to Washington at a time when they were selected by state legislators. Black men also served as secretary of state in Mississippi for nearly a decade after the Civil War. In 1870, 14 percent of the state Senate and 47 percent of the state House of Representatives were made up of Black men. By 1874, nearly 80 percent of the state House was Black. Because Reconstruction showed such promise in Mississippi, the backlash that followed was orchestrated, acute, and violent. A defining feature of Mississippi history is that white violence directly triggered an exodus . One historian estimates that from 1914 to 1920, during the Great Migration, one in five of the Black migrants leaving the South for economic opportunity, safety, dignity, and more came from Mississippi. White Mississippians waged yet more violence against Black folks who stayed, assassinating Medgar Evers, sickening and fatiguing Fannie Lou Hamer, and brutalizing everyday citizens into strange fruit . The remnants of that targeted violence are still visible today in the state’s stark inequality and lack of opportunity for Black Mississippians. But Colom’s campaign challenges the narrative that Mississippi should be defined through the lens of white harm, and that those with aspirations are better off leaving. On Wednesday night, Nadia Colom said to her and Scott’s twin girls, eighth-generation Mississippians, that she hoped the race reinforced the family motto to never quit, a value instilled in their father, who passed it to them. Persistence is a precious inheritance in a state that often ranks dead-last in indicators of prosperity, livelihood, health, well-being, and education. Scott Colom didn’t quit when donors wouldn’t answer the phone, when fewer than 10 people showed up at his first town hall, when it took eight days to rightfully claim his victory. For 200 years and counting, his ancestors didn’t quit on Mississippi, toiling and resisting on the lands that he traversed during his campaign. Now he is reaping the reward of remaining.

items.title: La Tunisie s’endette pour construire une autoroute vers l’Algérie
items.description: Le projet de construction d’une autoroute reliant la Tunisie à la frontière avec l’Algérie a franchi une nouvelle étape décisive, avec l’obtention par Tunis d’un financement de la Banque islamique de développement (BID). La nouvelle a été annoncée par le ministre tunisien de l’Économie et de la Planification, Samir Abdelhafidh, rapporte ce samedi la presse locale. La BID a donné une suite favorable à la demande tunisienne en septembre dernier et la convention de financement entre les deux parties sera signée en 2027, selon la même source. Le montant approuvé s’élève à 335,49 millions d’euros. Autoroute vers l’Algérie : un projet stratégique pour la Tunisie Devant les membres de l’Assemblée des représentants du peuple (ARP) et du Conseil national des régions et des districts réunis pour examiner le Budget 2027, le ministre tunisien a souligné l’importance stratégique de cette autoroute qui permettra de compléter jusqu’en Tunisie l’autoroute est-ouest algérienne. Cette autoroute va faciliter les déplacements routiers entre les deux pays d’autant que la Tunisie est la destination touristique préférée des Algériens. De nombreux Tunisiens se rendent régulièrement en Algérie pour notamment acheter des produits de large consommation qui bénéficient du soutien de l’État. À cela s’ajoute le développement des liens économiques et du commerce entre les deux pays. L’Algérie, qui compte 1605 km d’autoroutes et 145615 km de routes, a achevé son autoroute reliant l’est à l’ouest du pays sur plus de 1200 km. Pour la Tunisie, qui compte 743 kilomètres autoroutes, elle ambitionne de porter ce chiffre à 1 323 kilomètres à l’horizon 2035. L’article La Tunisie s’endette pour construire une autoroute vers l’Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Surgeon Dr Dakurah enters NPP parliamentary race in Nadowli-Kaleo
items.description: A surgeon, Dr Justine Dakurah, has declared his intention to contest the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) parliamentary primary in the Nadowli-Kaleo Constituency of the Upper West Region. He made the announcement on Friday, 13 November, at the party’s constituency office in Nadowli, where he addressed friends, party members, and some constituency executives. Dr Dakurah says his decision to enter politics is driven by a desire to address what he considers key development challenges in the constituency, including healthcare, education, sanitation, employment, and infrastructure. “My decision to enter politics is driven by a deep-seated commitment to service: Improving healthcare delivery, advancing grassroots development and giving the constituents a stronger voice and opportunities,” he said. He also criticised the development record of successive governments in the constituency, arguing that it had little to show despite being represented by the National Democratic Congress (NDC) since 1993. The constituency is currently represented by NDC MP Anthony Mwinkaara Sumah, who is serving his second term. Dr Dakurah has proposed establishing a scholarship fund for academically gifted but financially disadvantaged students, alongside initiatives to empower women and improve roads and healthcare delivery. He also called for unity within the NPP and urged prospective parliamentary candidates to run issue-based campaigns without resorting to personal attacks once they are cleared by the party to contest. Dr Dakurah trained at the University for Development Studies (UDS) Medical School in Tamale. He began his medical career as a medical officer at the Lawra Government Hospital, where he worked from 2014 to 2018. He subsequently moved to the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, where he undertook specialist training in surgery between 2019 and 2022. He returned to the Lawra Government Hospital in 2022 and worked there until 2024 before moving to the Tamale Teaching Hospital, where he is currently undertaking a fellowship training. He has also continued to provide surgical services at the Nadowli Government Hospital. His declaration comes after the party announced the opening nominations early this month for its parliamentary primaries ahead of the next general election. Three other people are reportedly seeking the party’s nomination in the constituency: Dr Elvis Botah, Dr Agape Kanyiri, and former parliamentary candidate Francis Xavier Kambotuu.

items.title: Kidnap: Police nab son over alleged N30m ransom demand from father
items.description: ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌‍⁠The Police Command in Ebonyi has arrested two suspects for allegedly staging a kidnapping and demanding a ransom of N30 million from the father of one of them. The suspects are Fortune Onuoha and his friend, Godspower Nkwo, popularly known as Hulk. The Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), SP Joshua Ukandu, disclosed this in a statement issued to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Saturday in Abakaliki. Ukandu said the incident was reported on Oct. 31, 2026, at about 10:30 p.m., when Onuoha’s father contacted the Command’s Control Room to report that his son had been abducted from his hostel in Ikwo Local Government Area of the state. He said the complainant also reported receiving view-once videos and voice notes showing his son tied up, alongside demands for N30 million ransom by the purported kidnappers. According to him, the abductors threatened to kill the victim if the ransom was not paid. The PPRO said that following the report, the command deployed operatives to conduct an intelligence-driven investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged abduction and identify those responsible. He said sustained surveillance and discreet investigative efforts led to a breakthrough on Nov. 5, when police operatives arrested the two suspects as they emerged from the room where they had been hiding. Ukandu quoted the Commissioner of Police in the state, Mrs Urunwa Okafor, as warning members of the public against staging kidnappings or making false claims of abduction. According to the PPRO, the commissioner said such acts inflicted severe emotional trauma on parents, guardians, and loved ones while diverting valuable police resources from addressing genuine security threats. She stressed that staging kidnappings and making false abduction claims were criminal offenses punishable under the law. The police commissioner urged members of the public to shun criminal activities and embrace lawful means of addressing their challenges. (NAN) The post Kidnap: Police nab son over alleged N30m ransom demand from father appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La Guinée : une histoire, une mémoire et une dimension panafricaine qui méritent le respect (Par Soninké Diané)
items.description: À certains blogueurs maliens, Burkinabè et à quelques intellectuels qui semblent vouloir réécrire l'histoire de nos pays au gré de leurs émotions et de leurs opinions, je voudrais rappeler quelques vérités historiques. L'histoire de la Guinée ne commence pas avec les polémiques sur les réseaux sociaux. Elle ne se construit pas non plus à partir des frustrations du moment. Le 28 septembre 1958, la Guinée fut le seul territoire africain de l'ensemble des territoires français d'outre-mer à rejeter, par référendum, la Constitution proposée et l'adhésion à la Communauté française. Les autres territoires concernés avaient voté oui. Le 2 octobre 1958, notre indépendance nationale était solennellement proclamée. Ce choix historique, porté par le peuple de Guinée et incarné par Ahmed Sékou Touré, n'était pas un simple geste politique. C'était un acte d'affirmation de la dignité, de la liberté et de la souveraineté d'un peuple. Nous ne nions absolument pas les contributions des progressistes africains et d'ailleurs, des intellectuels, des militants et des femmes et hommes de bonne volonté qui ont apporté leur soutien, parfois bénévolement, à la jeune République de Guinée. Nous leur devons reconnaissance et respect. Mais il faut également reconnaître que ce choix a eu un prix considérable. La Guinée a subi les conséquences économiques et politiques de sa rupture avec la France, connu des tentatives de déstabilisation et même une agression militaire en novembre 1970, lors de l'opération portugaise contre Conakry, avec la participation de forces d'exilés guinéens. Nous avons payé cher notre choix de souveraineté. Notre histoire est aussi celle des sacrifices, des résistances et des espoirs que notre indépendance a suscités auprès de nombreux peuples africains encore sous domination coloniale. Notre hymne national est révélateur de cet idéal. Nos engagements historiques et notre solidarité avec les mouvements de libération africains en sont également des témoignages. Cela ne signifie pas que la Guinée détient le monopole du panafricanisme, ni que les autres peuples africains n'ont pas leur propre histoire de lutte et de résistance. Le Mali, le Burkina Faso et les autres nations africaines ont aussi leurs héros, leurs sacrifices et leurs pages glorieuses. Mais personne ne devrait instrumentaliser le panafricanisme pour falsifier l'histoire ou contester à la Guinée le droit d'exercer sa souveraineté. Venons-en aux événements actuels concernant l'orpaillage à Siguiri. Il faut sortir des manipulations émotionnelles et des raccourcis dangereux. La décision des autorités guinéennes vise à mettre fin à l'exploitation artisanale anarchique et illégale, à protéger les ressources naturelles, les terres agricoles, les cours d'eau et l'environnement. Cette mesure a des conséquences sur les Guinéens eux-mêmes, avant même de toucher les ressortissants des autres pays africains présents dans les zones concernées. Elle ne doit donc pas être transformée en une confrontation entre nationalités. Nous avons le devoir de protéger notre patrimoine naturel. Les ressources de la Guinée appartiennent d'abord à la Nation guinéenne et leur exploitation doit respecter nos lois, préserver nos écosystèmes et profiter durablement aux générations futures. On peut discuter des modalités d'application d'une décision publique, demander davantage d'accompagnement aux populations affectées et dénoncer d'éventuels abus. C'est parfaitement légitime. Mais cela ne donne à personne le droit de présenter un acte de souveraineté comme une hostilité envers un peuple frère. Le panafricanisme ne doit pas être un instrument de pression contre les États africains. Il doit être une école de respect mutuel, de solidarité, de vérité historique et de responsabilité. La Guinée n'a pas besoin de dénigrer les autres nations pour faire respecter son histoire. Elle n'a pas non plus besoin de se justifier d'être souveraine. Je le dis avec conviction : la Guinée n'est pas simplement un pays qui parle du panafricanisme. Par son histoire, ses choix et les sacrifices consentis pour sa liberté, elle en incarne une dimension profondément symbolique. La Guinée est une terre de liberté, une terre de dignité et une terre d'espérance pour l'Afrique. Respectons nos histoires respectives et construisons ensemble notre avenir commun. items.title: Japan score in injury time to stun Brazil 3-2 in Singapore
items.description: Substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto netted his first international goal with a late winner as Japan edged Brazil 3-2 in a thrilling friendly at the National Stadium in Singapore on Saturday. A brilliant brace by Vinicius Junior had erased a two-goal deficit after strikes by Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura put the Samurai Blue 2-0 up in the opening 19 minutes. But Sakamoto was in the right place to fire home after latching on to Kodai Sano’s deflected effort in stoppage time to give the Asian side a dramatic victory in front of 38,688 fans. In the first meeting between the teams since Brazil’s 2-1 win in the round of 32 at the World Cup in June, the Samurai Blue seized the early initiative with two goals in a torrid four-minute spell. On 15 minutes, a through ball by Ritsu Doan was picked up just inside the Brazilian half by Kubo who showed quick feet to cut inside Jair before firing a low effort past goalkeeper Pedro Morisco. Japan added another shortly afterwards after some fine work by Shuto Nakano, who broke down the right flank and centred for an unmarked Nakamura to calmly place a right-footed shot into the bottom corner of the net. Brazil responded with a magnificent goal by Vinicius in the 33rd minute. Zion Suzuki had made an excellent stop to deny Estevao when he bore down on goal, but the Japan goalkeeper could do little when the ball fell to Vinicius who found the top corner with a right-footed diagonal drive. Suzuki made good stops to deny Brazilian debutant Andre just before half-time and skipper Raphinha after the interval as Japan clung to their narrow lead. But the Selecao were not to be denied and Vinicius put them back on level terms in the 75th minute with another fine finish as he cut in from the left flank and launched a low right-footed effort that found the net off the right post. Brazil went close to grabbing the winner as substitute Endrick rocked the crossbar with a fierce effort and Joao Gomes sent a low shot narrowly wide. But in stoppage time, an effort by Kodai Sano took a fortunate bounce off a defender and fell nicely for Sakamoto to send the ball past Pedro Morisco. Brazil appealed for a foul in the build-up to the goal but VAR upheld the goal and Raphinha and manager Carlo Ancelotti were shown red card for their protests. Japan head coach Hajime Moriyasu is expected to step down after a friendly against Paraguay next Tuesday, but the 58-year-old is looking forward to handing over to successor Go Oiwa after a performance he described as the best of his tenure. “I’m happy that I can say that today’s match was the best match in my eight-year tenure,” he said. “While we couldn’t beat Brazil in the World Cup, we managed to show today what we could have done, and it will be a good build-up for the team for the future. “Now I need to pass the baton to the next coach, and that’s all I am focusing on.” For Ancelotti, the work will go after what he saw as an encouraging performance by his youthful side. “Apart from the result, I think for 70 minutes we played well,” said the Italian. “We played what we wanted to do, play with intensity. I am satisfied with the game we played, apart from the start, which was not good.” The post Japan score in injury time to stun Brazil 3-2 in Singapore appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: FEC : les décaissements de prêts grimpent à 2,9 MMDH
items.description: Portés par la mobilité urbaine et interurbaine, les décaissements de prêts du FEC bondissent de 1 805 à 2 908 MDH en un an. Le PNB, lui, fait du surplace à 490 MDH : la hausse de l’activité ne fait que compenser la baisse des taux appliqués aux Collectivités Territoriales depuis janvier 2025. La dynamique des investissements territoriaux a eu un effet positif sur l’activité de prêts du Fonds d’équipement communal (FEC) à fin septembre 2026. Les indicateurs financiers du troisième trimestre font état d’engagements de prêts de 2 870 MDH, contre 2 708 MDH à fin septembre 2025, et de décaissements de 2 908 MDH, contre 1 805 MDH à la même période de l’année précédente. Ces financements portent principalement sur un programme d’investissement dédié à la mobilité urbaine et interurbaine, que la Banque présente comme un levier structurant d’attractivité des territoires. Les Conseils Régionaux en concentrent l’essentiel : ils ont représenté plus de 76% du volume global des engagements de prêts et plus de 88% de celui des décaissements à fin septembre 2026. Les créances sur la clientèle ont, pour leur part, enregistré une progression de près de 5% en glissement annuel, pour s’établir à 28 108 MDH à fin septembre 2026. Elles s’élevaient à 26 850 MDH à fin septembre 2025 et à 27 614 MDH à fin décembre 2025. Le produit net bancaire (PNB) ressort à 490 MDH au terme des neuf premiers mois de 2026, à un niveau comparable à celui de la même période de 2025, où il atteignait 491 MDH. Sur le seul troisième trimestre, il s’établit à 163 MDH, soit le même montant qu’un an auparavant. Cette stabilité s’explique principalement par la progression de l’activité de prêts, qui compense l’impact de la baisse des taux appliqués aux financements consentis aux Collectivités Territoriales à partir du 1er janvier 2025. Sur le volet environnemental et social, la Banque intègre la gestion des risques environnementaux, sociaux et climatiques dans ses processus d’évaluation et de décision à travers son Système de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale (SGES). Ce dispositif, aligné sur les standards internationaux, s’inscrit dans une démarche d’amélioration continue. Il se reflète dans le profil des projets engagés à fin septembre 2026 : plus de 97% relèvent des catégories C ou D de la grille de notation E&S, correspondant à des niveaux de risques minimes et faibles. La catégorie C représente 62% de ces projets, la catégorie D 35% et la catégorie B 3%. Du côté des ressources, l’encours des ressources d’emprunt atteint 23 616 MDH à fin septembre 2026, contre 22 908 MDH à fin décembre 2025 et 21 299 MDH à fin septembre 2025. Dans leur répartition, les emprunts financiers intérieurs pèsent 33%, contre 40% un an plus tôt, tandis que les emprunts financiers extérieurs passent de 24% à 26% et les emprunts obligataires de 31% à 33%. Dans le cadre de sa stratégie financière, le FEC poursuit ses efforts de diversification et de pérennisation de ses sources de financement, en veillant à mobiliser des ressources adaptées aux caractéristiques de son activité et aux besoins croissants des Collectivités Territoriales. Il s’attache également à développer de nouveaux partenariats financiers nationaux et internationaux en vue d’obtenir des conditions de refinancement optimales. À l’international, cette orientation s’est notamment concrétisée par le renforcement du partenariat stratégique avec la Banque Africaine de Développement (BAD). En juillet 2026, les deux institutions ont signé un deuxième accord de prêt d’un montant de 150 millions d’euros, faisant suite à un premier financement de 100 millions d’euros conclu en mars 2024. Le FEC y voit le témoignage de la confiance renouvelée de la BAD et d’un engagement commun en faveur d’un développement territorial durable, inclusif et résilient. Enfin, les fonds propres réglementaires de la Banque ont atteint 6 839 MDH à fin septembre 2026, dont 5 839 MDH de capital Tier one. Ils lui permettent de continuer à consolider son assise financière et de renforcer sa capacité à accompagner les besoins croissants des acteurs territoriaux. The post FEC : les décaissements de prêts grimpent à 2,9 MMDH appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Tinubu met Nigeria in intensive care unit, Mutfwang says
items.description: … Pledges Plateau’s support for President’s re-election, seeks assistance for IDPs, stadium By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has said President Bola Tinubu met Nigeria in an intensive care unit when he assumed office but has gradually moved the country into recovery through his administration’s policies. Mutfwang stated this on Saturday while speaking at the APC North-Central Presidential Campaign Rally at the Zaria Road Stadium, Jos, where he declared Plateau State’s support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The governor said, “You met Nigeria in the intensive care unit, and through the policies you have administered, like a drug, you have been able to bring Nigeria out of the intensive care unit. We are now in recovery.” “We are confident that if you continue, we will not only recover but prosper as well. That is why we are determined that in the 2027 election, there is no alternative for us. We will stick with you and go with you.” He described Tinubu as a friend of Plateau State and the North-Central region, citing the Federal Government’s interventions in road infrastructure, education and healthcare. “We consider you as a friend of Plateau State and North-Central Nigeria in general. You have demonstrated your love for our state and our region through the developmental strides we have seen in road infrastructure, education and healthcare.” “On the Plateau, students in tertiary institutions have received assistance through the NELFUND scheme to the tune of over N11 billion. You have approved the road from Akwanga to Jos. You have also approved the road from Jos to Shendam, right through to Ebonyi. We are truly grateful,” he said. Mutfwang also commended the President’s wife, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, for her support to the people of Plateau State, recalling her visit to the state with gifts. “Your dear wife, our mother, is a darling of the Plateau people. We now know that we have a mother in Aso Rock. When she came visiting us, she did not come empty-handed. Like a good mother, she came with a bag full of gifts for our people, and we will always be grateful,” he said. Recalling his promise to reciprocate Tinubu’s kindness during the President’s previous visit, the governor said the time had come for Plateau people to demonstrate their appreciation through their votes. “The time has come and the time is now. By the grace of God, we are going to show our gratitude come January 16, 2027, because we have seen a man who loves us.” “When Plateau takes a direction, many other communities that share affinity with it will also follow suit. We are confident that the votes we will give Mr President in this election will be unprecedented,” he said. On security, Mutfwang commended the Federal Government for its support, saying the state had recorded significant progress in tackling insecurity in the last three months. “In the last three months particularly, we have made tremendous progress in dealing with insurgency. Like you have often said, we will defeat insurgency, and already we can see victory on the way.” “With commitment and sustainability, we will eliminate these enemies of peace and progress, and we are confident that you will lead us in that direction,” he said. The governor, however, appealed to Tinubu to support the state in facilitating the return of internally displaced persons to their ancestral communities. “We will continue to solicit your help, Mr President, to make sure that our people who are internally displaced return to their ancestral homes. “We will be approaching you with a Marshall Plan for the return of our people to their ancestral homes. It is going to require substantial intervention from you, and we are confident that what you have done before, you will do again,” he said. Mutfwang also appealed to the President to assist in completing the Zaria Road Stadium, describing it as a facility whose construction began about 40 years ago. “Mr President, I will be pleading with you on behalf of the Plateau people. Please roll away our reproach. We need your help to make this stadium one of the international stadiums in Nigeria. I am sure it will become a symbol of pride for you when this is done,” he said He further disclosed that his administration had established an employment hub expected to provide jobs for 2,000 young people, alongside a technology hub designed to support security operations. “We have created an employment hub for 2,000 young people who will be working in America and Europe from the comfort of their homes here in Jos. “We have also created another hub for technology so that we can deploy effective technology for the detection of criminals,” he said. The governor added that additional buses had been procured to ease transportation challenges facing residents of the state. The post Tinubu met Nigeria in intensive care unit, Mutfwang says appeared first on Vanguard News .

Obuasi Sexual Abuse Case: No teacher will be shielded if evidence proves wrongdoing – Haruna Iddrisu
items.description: The Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, has assured that no teacher implicated in the allegations of sexual misconduct at Obuasi Senior High School (SHS) will be shielded from prosecution if evidence establishes their culpability. He said the government was committed to ensuring accountability in the matter, which he described as a scar for the government, adding that appropriate action would be taken against anyone found to have breached the law. Speaking at the 150th anniversary celebration of Mfantsipim School on Saturday, November 14, Mr Iddrisu said the evidence currently available to the Ministry of Education pointed to what could constitute a prima facie case, but stressed that the Ministry and the Ghana Education Service (GES) did not have the authority to determine criminal guilt. “Matters relating to Obuasi SHTS remain a scar for government. Let me assure you that nobody will be shielded. Once the evidence is available, government will take appropriate steps to prosecute and make sure that we exact the exact punishment on persons that are culpable,” he said. “The evidence before us points to what the courts may describe as a prima facie case, but since the Ministry of Education and GES are not competent courts, I will accordingly refer, and have referred, the matter to the Police CID, the Attorney-General and the Minister for the Interior to take consequential actions that bring any teacher to the discipline of the law,” he stated. The case has generated considerable debate about student protection, teacher conduct and the responsibility of educational authorities to ensure that schools remain safe spaces for children. Background The Obuasi Senior High School case has attracted national attention following allegations of sexual misconduct involving students and the school’s former headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai. The controversy has triggered calls for accountability, stronger safeguarding measures and improved systems for reporting and investigating abuse in educational institutions. The headmaster was suspended following the allegations, while investigations and other interventions were initiated by the relevant authorities. The case has also renewed discussions about the protection of students, the responsibility of school management and the need for effective mechanisms to prevent abuse and ensure that allegations are handled promptly. Mr Iddrisu’s latest comments reaffirm the government’s commitment to pursuing accountability, while leaving the determination of criminal responsibility to the appropriate investigative and judicial authorities.

items.title: India stun Pakistan by one wicket in last-ball U-19 Asia Cup final thriller
items.description: Mohit Ulva and Chigurupati Venkata held their nerve to guide India to a dramatic one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the ACC Men’s U-19 Asia Cup final, chasing down a target of 338 on the final ball at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Muscat on Saturday. India were staring at defeat at 252 for eight in the 42nd over before Ulva and Manal Chauhan revived their hopes with a 57-run partnership for the ninth wicket. Chauhan struck three fours and three sixes in his 32-ball 47 before falling at 309 in the 48th over, leaving India needing 29 from the final 16 deliveries. Ulva and Venkata then added an unbeaten 30 runs for the last wicket to take India home. With eight runs required in the final over, Ulva, who finished unbeaten on 49 off 26 balls, including five fours and three sixes, struck the winning boundary off Ahmed Hussain’s final delivery. Venkata remained not out on 11 off eight balls as India finished at 339 for nine in 50 overs. Captain Lakshya Raichandani had earlier top-scored with 80 off 101 balls, while Aaryavir Sehwag contributed 58 from 61 deliveries. The pair provided India with a strong start, putting on 95 for the opening wicket before Sehwag was dismissed in the 18th over. Pakistan, however, kept striking at regular intervals to regain control. Raichandani departed at 217 in the 37th over, and India lost their eighth wicket just one run later, with the scoreboard reading 252. Rizwanullah was Pakistan’s most successful bowler with three for 53 in his 10 overs, while Niqab Shafiq claimed two for 57. The defeat denied defending champions Pakistan a successful title defence after they had entered the final unbeaten, winning all three group matches, including an earlier victory over India, before overcoming Bangladesh in the semi-final. Earlier, Pakistan posted 337 for nine after opting to bat, with Usman Khan scoring a century and Abdul Qadir and captain Farhan Yousaf making valuable half-centuries. Usman and Hayam Khan provided Pakistan with a steady start, putting on 62 for the opening wicket. Hayam struck four boundaries in his 23-ball 21 before falling in the ninth over. Usman then combined with Qadir in a commanding 135-run partnership for the second wicket. Qadir provided the acceleration with an attacking 80 off just 54 balls, hitting three fours and eight sixes before being dismissed on the last ball of the 27th over with Pakistan at 197 for two. Usman continued to anchor the innings, reaching his second century of the tournament. The left-hander struck 107 off 111 deliveries, including 11 fours and three sixes, before falling in the 37th over with Pakistan at 240 for three. Farhan maintained the momentum with a 60-ball 63, including four fours and three sixes. He added 59 runs for the fourth wicket with Ahmed Hussain, who contributed 17 off 20 balls. Pakistan had looked set for a total in excess of 350 after reaching 204 for two at the halfway stage. However, India’s bowlers pulled things back in the closing overs, restricting Pakistan to 337 for nine. Kavya Paresh Patel led the Indian attack with four for 68 in his 10 overs, while Venkata, who came into the side in place of the injured Ishan Sood, claimed three for 40 from five overs. Arjun Rajput took one wicket for 43. Ulva was named player of the match for his decisive contribution in the chase, while Sehwag received the player of the tournament award.
